title: fix: show fuse ratings once in component details
description: Fixes duplicate display of fuse ratings in component details by mapping display fields and hiding duplicates.
body: The fuse popup on [my USB-C control dial board](https://tscircuit.com/krishnax12/usb-c-control-dial) shows each rating twice: numeric `current_rating_amps` / `voltage_rating_volts` rows and separate `display_current_rating` / `display_voltage_rating` rows. Map these two differently named display fields into the existing component-details formatter and hide their duplicate rows. A 0.5 A / 24 V fuse now shows `current_rating_amps: "500mA"` and `voltage_rating_volts: "24V"` once each. Missing or blank display text still falls back to the numeric rating, including zero. Related repro: #297. This branch enables the existing TSX/actual-tooltip regression test and adds a minimal Cosmos fixture. The repro fails without the implementation change and passes with it. No dependency or Circuit JSON changes. Validation: 54 tests pass; TypeScript, changed-file formatting, and Cosmos export build pass. Clicked F1 in the local Cosmos viewer and verified each rating appears once. Cosmos-preview: ## Deployment-link ## [View Cosmos preview](https://schematic-viewer-1fvj53py2-tscircuit.vercel.app/?fixtureId=%7B%22path%22%3A%22examples%2Fexample39-fuse-component-details.fixture.tsx%22%7D) — click F1 to inspect the ratings. Same TSX input, rendered by the actual tooltip before and after the fix: ```tsx ``` | Before | After | | --- | --- | | ![Duplicate fuse ratings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/schematic-viewer/98ee7689faf74dd403a8c0aa2cde58d5a7de311f/fuse-popup-before.png) | ![Each fuse rating shown once with units](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KrishnaX12/schematic-viewer/98ee7689faf74dd403a8c0aa2cde58d5a7de311f/fuse-popup-after.png) |

title: feat: search PCB components and briefly highlight results
description: Adds a Search button to the PCB toolbar that allows users to search for placed components by name, highlighting the selected component for three seconds after selection.
body:
Adds a Search button to the PCB toolbar. Search lists placed components by name, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace. Clicking a result or confirming the active suggestion with Enter switches to its layer, smoothly centers and zooms over 450 ms with surrounding board context, and highlights it for three seconds. Clicking Search again, Escape, or an outside click closes the panel.

The input keeps focus when clicked. Renamed source components refresh the search results even when PCB geometry stays unchanged. Manual interaction cancels the animation; reduced-motion preferences use an instant transition. Existing controller focus behavior is preserved.

The UI is isolated in `ComponentSearch`, with animation and highlight lifecycle in `usePcbComponentSearchFocus`. Both reuse existing component bounds and transform-animation utilities. This follows Seve's merged-PR feedback on extracting behavior from large viewer files (#733, #741) and reusing shared types/helpers (#738, #741).

## Validation
- `npm run build`: bundle and TypeScript declarations pass.
- `tsc --noEmit`: full repository typecheck passes.
- `bun test`: 67 tests pass.
- Playwright component-focus suite: input clicks/typing, filtering, empty results, smooth zoom progression, centering, layer selection, highlight timeout/reset, cancellation, reduced motion, source-name updates, and existing controller behavior pass.
- Biome checks pass for the new components/hook and revised viewer/test files; `git diff --check` passes.

## Reproduction
1. Check out `feat/component-search`, install dependencies, and run `npm start`.
2. Open the `2026/pcb-viewer-controller` Cosmos fixture.
3. Hover over the viewer, click Search, click inside its text box, and type `u` (U1 and U2) or `u2` (U2 only).
4. Click U2 bottom: the layer changes, the viewer smoothly pans and zooms to U2 with surrounding context, and the blue outline disappears after three seconds.
5. Select the same result again within three seconds to restart the highlight. Pan or scroll during a transition to cancel it.
6. Check Search toggle, Escape, outside click, Enter selection, and a name with no matches.


## Host compatibility verification

Manually verified minified production-mode builds using the actual RunFrame and tscircuit.com PCB wrapper source at desktop and mobile widths with Tailwind base styles, including the website's Click to Interact gate. Search input focus/typing, selection, contextual zoom, highlight expiry, and Escape dismissal passed. No additional host integration test files or scripts are included.

This verifies the canvas wrapper integration with the PR package, not the live deployed website or the complete RunFrame/WebGPU application. Production rollout requires merging and releasing this viewer, updating and rebuilding/releasing RunFrame's bundled distributions, then updating tscircuit.com's viewer and RunFrame dependencies and lockfile and deploying. Current production packages do not yet contain this unmerged feature.


Arrow Up/Down now move through suggestions with wraparound, visibly select and scroll the active suggestion into view, and immediately preview it with the existing smooth zoom and highlight without closing search. Keyboard focus stays in the combobox; Enter confirms the active suggestion. The focus outline now follows each component's local dimensions and rotation rather than its axis-aligned bounds. Verified manually in the browser at 45° and 90°, including arrow navigation and empty results. Existing browser-suite selectors were updated for the accessible combobox/listbox roles; no new tests were added.

title: fix: bundle renderer with pcb_stackup metadata support
description: Fixes the renderer to support pcb_stackup metadata, preventing the WebGPU worker from stopping prematurely when rendering boards with this metadata.
body:
An eight-layer `<board thickness={1.2} fabricatorPreset="jlcpcb_standard">` emits `pcb_stackup`. The currently bundled renderer rejects that metadata, so the WebGPU worker stops before its first frame even though the board has no circuit errors.

Update the renderer tarball pin and lockfile from **0.0.10 to 0.0.11**, which includes the merged metadata fix. No viewer runtime code changes or local package patches are needed. The [renderer version comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/compare/v0.0.10...v0.0.11) also includes the previously merged handling of trace segments inside copper pours. The diff is **3 additions / 3 deletions** across the package manifest and lockfile.

The native TSX reproduction and regression coverage already landed in [renderer reproduction #90](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/pull/90) and [stacked fix #91](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/pull/91):

- [TSX board fixture](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/blob/v0.0.11/tests/fixtures/pcb-stackup.tsx): two resistors and a routed trace; core generates all Circuit JSON.
- [Regression test](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/blob/v0.0.11/tests/pcb-stackup.test.ts): no diagnostics and unchanged geometry with stackup metadata.
- [Compiler allowlist](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/blob/v0.0.11/lib/compile-circuit.ts#L371): recognizes stackup as non-geometric metadata. Unsupported shapes retain diagnostics.
- [Publication run](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/actions/runs/40749478951): published the tested merge commit `4ba7844` as 0.0.11. That commit also has passing renderer and parity CI.

To reproduce interactively with sibling renderer/viewer checkouts, install the renderer's dev dependencies and generate its native fixture into the viewer's ignored transport directory:

```sh
mkdir -p tests/webgpu/actual
bun ../circuit-json-webgpu/tests/fixtures/pcb-stackup.tsx > tests/webgpu/actual/stackup.circuit.json
bun run build
bunx vite --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5179
```

Open `http://127.0.0.1:5179/tests/webgpu/?circuitJsonUrl=/tests/webgpu/actual/stackup.circuit.json`. Main fails with the stackup diagnostic; this branch renders. Add `&scenario=canvas` for the Canvas control. The upstream TSX fixture also reproduces with its default thickness; the focused browser check used 1.2 mm.

Validation: renderer typecheck/build and 111 unit tests pass; viewer typecheck/build and 82 unit tests pass against the published package. The full viewer WebGPU browser suite passes with SwiftShader. A focused check of the published package verifies an actual worker frame, no errors, pixel-identical rendering with/without stackup metadata, and continued rejection of unsupported pad shapes. The local broad renderer visual run stalled before producing snapshots and was stopped; it is not counted as a passing check.

title: Remove the remaining transitive JSCAD CDN dependency
description: Removes the transitive dependency on the JSCAD CDN by updating the circuit-json-to-gltf package version, ensuring that installations do not rely on the CDN and pass tests without external network access.
body:
`bun add -d @types/react tscircuit` still fails when npm is allowed but `jscdn.tscircuit.com` is blocked. The published dependency chain is `tscircuit@0.0.3052 → circuit-json-to-gltf@0.0.163 → jscad-electronics@0.0.242 → @tscircuit/jscad` at the CDN tarball URL. Updating `jscad-fiber` alone leaves this second path intact; `^0.0.163` does not admit `0.0.164`.

Update to `circuit-json-to-gltf@^0.0.164` and refresh the lockfile. That release uses `jscad-electronics@0.0.243`, `jscad-fiber@0.0.93`, and `@tscircuit/jscad@0.0.6` from npm. Extend the existing packed-package installation test to reject tscircuit CDN URLs in the resulting consumer lockfile.

Validation on macOS arm64 with Bun 1.4.4:
- Reproduced the original published-package failure with npm allowed and the tscircuit CDN returning 403.
- Repacked the integrity-verified public `tscircuit@0.0.3052` artifact with exactly the proposed dependency change. A fresh consumer installation passed in 34.00 seconds with the CDN blocked; no connection to that host occurred and its lockfile contained no CDN URL. Native installation also contacted GitHub release hosts.
- The updated exporter generated a valid 17,456-byte GLB with external network access disabled.
- The packed npm consumer regression test passed in 50.22 seconds with only npm connections through the proxy.
- Formatting of the changed test and `git diff --check` passed.

Coordinate with https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5064: core's version synchronization otherwise restores `^0.0.163`. The repository development lockfile still contains the older auto-installed `tscircuit` peer's graph; the new regression checks the actual packed consumer graph.

Related standalone fix: https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5633 avoids this redundant installation by default. These changes need publication before the public install command benefits.

title: Represent collisions during assembly explosion movements
description: Add cad_explosion_collision_error for an explosion move that enters a CAD part or PCB substrate, and cad_explosion_collision_check_warning for unsupportedinvalid geometry or a failed check, allowing consumers to distinguish confirmed collisions from incomplete coverage.
body:
Add `cad_explosion_collision_error` for an explosion move that enters a CAD part or PCB substrate. Reference the executing stage/move, moving CAD component, and obstacle; record newly swept intersection volume in mm³. body:

title: Add typed default-family resolution for bare passive footprint sizes
description: Adds a typed default-family option and a public string resolver to handle bare passive sizes without duplicating size-token parsing.
body:
Bare passive sizes currently always resolve to the resistor family. A caller that knows it is rendering a capacitor or diode must duplicate Footprinter's size-token parsing to qualify strings such as `0805`. This adds a typed default-family option and a public string resolver so Footprinter owns that grammar.

```ts
fp.string("0805_polarized", { defaultFamily: "cap" }).circuitJson()
// Same geometry and polarity marks as cap0805_polarized.

resolvePassiveFootprintDefinition("0805_pw0.8mm", { defaultFamily: "cap" })
// "cap0805_pw0.8mm"

resolvePassiveFootprintDefinition("res0805", { defaultFamily: "cap" })
// "res0805" — explicit families take precedence.
```

The shared resolver handles existing four- and five-digit bare sizes, metric forms, dimensions, and modifiers. Both `fp.string` and the exported `string` parser accept `FootprinterStringOptions`; `PassiveFootprintFamily` is the union `"res" | "cap" | "diode" | "led"`. Callers such as core can choose the family based on the component type without copying the numeric-size regex.

Existing calls keep the resistor default and normalized authored `params().string`. Existing silkscreen differences between bare resistor sizes and explicit `res` strings are preserved. The string resolver only qualifies the family; it does not validate sizes or normalize named-package aliases. Component policy and Circuit JSON metadata are unchanged.

Validation:
- `bun test`: **710 pass, 0 fail**, including 28 new API/regression tests.
- 11 new SVG snapshots, visually checked, cover families, metric/five-digit sizes, units, capacitor polarity/transforms, and diode terminal mapping.
- `bunx biome format .` and `bun run build` pass.
- Consumer TypeScript check against emitted declarations passes, including rejection of unsupported default families.

This is the Footprinter API needed to remove duplicated bare-size parsing from [core #4959](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4959). This PR does not change core.

Retain `nonpolarized` in the base schema and builder types, and carry it to the shared diode fabrication helper. Skip generation there when the flag is true. Cover passive LED/diode families, SOD/MELF/SMA/SMB/SMC families, flat-lead diode packages, LED2835/5050 and explicitly polarized two-pad smdpads. Default output and `nonpolarized(false)` retain existing symbols; unrelated fabrication records, including DIP pin labels, remain untouched.

Validation:
- New regression fails on main because six fabrication records remain for a neutral diode definition.
- Covers 31 footprint definitions, default/false/true behavior, identical copper and courtyards, builder/string parity, origin/pin1location/nosilkscreen composition, and preservation of unrelated fabrication labels. Includes before/after SVG snapshots.
- Full suite: 681 tests pass, zero failures, including network-backed KiCad parity tests. Package/declaration build and source formatting pass.
- Combined integration with capacitor fabrication PR #977 and tscircuit/core#4959 passes both terminal mappings, all four rotations and both PCB sides for capacitor marks; neutral SOD suppression and a single LED symbol also pass.

Independent of #977 and based directly on main. This completes the neutral-definition behavior requested by tscircuit/core#4959 without adding metadata or deleting arbitrary fabrication records.

title: fix: generate fabrication polarity marks for polarized capacitors

body:
`cap0805_polarized` currently emits a printed silkscreen plus but no fabrication-layer polarity records. When core delegates fabrication artwork to Footprinter (tscircuit/core#4959), the capacitor's fabrication indication disappears.

Generate three fabrication paths forming a plus at the positive pad and a minus at the negative pad. Use the resolved positive/negative terminal centres for SMT and through-hole footprints, with mark dimensions scaled to pad spacing. Generate the marks in footprint-local coordinates so existing origin and pin1location transforms apply once. Existing silkscreen, copper, pin numbering and courtyards are unchanged; ordinary/nonpolarized capacitors remain unmarked, and `nosilkscreen` retains the fabrication marks.

The README shows `Circuit.add(TSX)` → `renderUntilSettled()` → `getCircuitJson()` → `CadViewer circuitJson`.

Two existing core limitations prevent moving the original PCB build wholly to the newest renderer: its ground-pour guard still rejects changed geometry, and importing its standalone JSON through `<subcircuit circuitJson>` fails on unsupported `simple_fuse`. Neither guard is bypassed and no board parts are dropped. Also preserves the JSCAD `cad_component.color` fix needed for assembly appearance.

Raw board exports still contain 201 records rejected by the schema (versus 200 standalone), involving existing null IDs/anchor alignment and numeric display offsets; new explosion records validate. body:
`assembly.bolt` is defined in props but has no core implementation. It now renders and fastens to actual PCB holes or mechanical reference datums:

```tsx
<assembly.bolt
  name="B1"
  model="hexsocketbolt_m3_l10mm"
  fastenedTo=".CONTROL > .H1"
/>
<assembly.bolt
  name="B2"
  model="hexsocketbolt_m3_l10mm"
  fastenedTo=".CONTROL > .H2 > .bottom"
/>
```

Model strings such as `hexsocketbolt_m3_l10mm` use the existing modelprinter definitions and modelcdn URLs directly. Dimensional bolts support socket, hex, pan and countersunk heads through modelprinter definitions. Unsupported dimensional specifications produce a named error.

- Named `hole` and `platedhole` targets use their finalized emitted PCB centers after layout, rotation and translation. A bare hole target seats on the top surface; `.top` and `.bottom` select the surface explicitly.
- CSS selectors and compact named paths work. `mountGap`, signed `mountOffset`, an optional explicit `mountFace`, tilted parent frames, and device scope use the existing mounting solver. The default bolt mating origin is its head seating plane.
- Mechanical holes and slots use authored reference datums at their physical seating locations. This does not infer hole centers from arbitrary imported meshes.
- Bolts participate in assembly explosion targets, including serialized stages and moves in a tilted owner frame.
- The gantry example now uses `.ROOT > .rail`.

All new snapshots use real JSCAD Electronics fasteners with recognizable fixtures. Each image was visually inspected; local pinned meshes omit thread tessellation for repeatable rendering.

| Visual coverage | Snapshot |
| --- | --- |
| Plain/plated holes, translated/rotated hole pattern, top/bottom seating, 2 mm gap | [PCB fastening](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/884aad71f91c8e50f3baacdcfbdbfc4c329fb69c/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-bolt-hole-mounting-annotated.snap.png) |
| Tilted bracket, slotted hole datums, signed offsets and exploded bolts | [Mechanical fastening](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/884aad71f91c8e50f3baacdcfbdbfc4c329fb69c/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-bolt-reference-mounting-annotated.snap.png) |
| Dimensional socket, hex, pan and countersunk heads | [Head types](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/884aad71f91c8e50f3baacdcfbdbfc4c329fb69c/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-bolt-head-types-annotated.snap.png) |

Validation: all 109 assembly tests passed, including four new tests and actual exported GLB bounds. Full TypeScript check, ESM/declaration build, repository formatting, and diff checks passed. The live modelcdn M3 x 10 GLB was also fetched and exported to verify its real seating origin and shaft length.

The canonical-string follow-up removed shorthand expansion, updated the examples and snapshots, and passed all four bolt tests (65 assertions).

title: Support CSS face mounting and relative offsets on assembly parts
description: Generic parts and subassemblies can now use face constraints to position their geometry and children. mountedTo accepts CSS selectors or compact identity paths; mountOffset.xy moves along the target faces tangents and mountGap sets normal clearance. Geometry-less containers and the subassembly alias work too. CSS resolution includes explicit surfaces, generated JSCAD datums, and NEMA faces, with device scope isolation and named errors for missingambiguous targets and cycles. Boards retain PCB anchoring, and motors inherit mounted container frames. The complete rigid frame reaches CAD children and emitted reference surfaces; CAD Euler composition now matches the exported GLB for tilted models. Uses published tscircuitprops0.0.716 from props 967. No absolute cadPosition or cadRotation props are added.
body:
Generic parts and subassemblies can now use face constraints to position their geometry and children. `mountedTo` accepts CSS selectors or compact identity paths; `mountOffset.x/y` moves along the target face's tangents and `mountGap` sets normal clearance. Geometry-less containers and the subassembly alias work too.

CSS resolution includes explicit surfaces, generated JSCAD datums, and NEMA faces, with device scope isolation and named errors for missing/ambiguous targets and cycles. Boards retain PCB anchoring, and motors inherit mounted container frames. The complete rigid frame reaches CAD children and emitted reference surfaces; CAD Euler composition now matches the exported GLB for tilted models.

Uses published `@tscircuit/props@0.0.716` from [props #967](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/967). No absolute `cadPosition` or `cadRotation` props are added.

```tsx
<assembly.subassembly
  name="Z_MODULE"
  mountedTo=".BRIDGE > .rail"
  mountFace="base"
  mountOffset={{ x: "10mm", y: "-5mm" }}
  mountGap="2mm"
>
  {/* Local reference surfaces and nested parts */}
</assembly.subassembly>
```

All six visual snapshot files in this PR now use recognizable mechanical assemblies. Motors, screws, SOIC8 and pin headers are pinned JSCAD Electronics models; the gantry, brackets, spacers and enclosure have realistic machining features. Large model views, part-color legends, close/underside cameras, and gap/motion callouts make each case readable. Every revised image was visually inspected. [Model provenance and regeneration instructions](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/0075fefd1a66a609ed16396e329489ad2a20a1c5/tests/assembly/fixtures/mechanical-assembly-models.md) are included.

Automatic dependency synchronization copies `circuit-json-to-gltf` from core into the top-level `tscircuit` package. The installed exporter produced a valid 17,456-byte GLB with external network access disabled. This change updates one dependency version; the full core suite was not run.

title: fix: correct SMD bounds that block native A13 DDR routing

title: fix: preserve SMT pad solder mask settings during Circuit JSON import
description: Fixes the preservation of SMT pad solder mask settings during Circuit JSON import, ensuring that the PCB antenna retains its masked feed pad and that Gerber export remains accurate after import.
body:
Saving and importing a board now preserves SMT pad solder-mask coverage and explicit margins. Core's `ANT1` PCB antenna keeps its automatically generated 0.8 × 0.8 mm feed pad masked; Gerber export stays at zero openings after import.

Forward `is_covered_with_solder_mask` and `soldermask_margin` into the rectangle, circle, pill, rotated-pill and rotated-rectangle constructors. The polygon branch already preserves them. The production change is ten lines.

This PR builds on #4972 in native GitHub stack #4976. It fixes the importer, restores regular `test` calls for both regressions marked `test.failing` in the repro layer, and updates one antenna-board snapshot. The numeric regression still covers all six pad shapes on both layers, positive/zero/negative margins, omitted defaults, and saved-JSON immutability.

Validation: both round-trip regressions pass as regular tests; `tsc --noEmit`, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass. Keeping `test.failing` with the fix correctly reports both tests as unexpected passes. Gerber validation confirms the antenna stays at zero openings; native rectangle/circle cases preserve coverage, signed/zero margins and aperture dimensions.

The single updated snapshot shows the imported antenna with its feed pad still masked. The faulty version is in #4972.

![Imported antenna with preserved feed mask](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/7638d13a8ec8c3bfef77bb189dac2d95cad02d45/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-antenna-mask-round-trip-imported-board-pcb.snap.svg)

title: repro: saved-board import exposes a PCB antenna's masked feed pad
description: Fixes a bug where saving and re-importing a board causes a PCB antennas feed pad to be incorrectly exposed instead of masked.
body:
Saving and re-importing a board exposes the masked feed pad of Core's PCB antenna component.

The reproduction uses `<antenna name="ANT1" antennaShape="2.4ghz_meandered_monopole" />`. The component generates its own antenna copper, keepout and masked 0.8 × 0.8 mm feed pad. After JSON serialization and public `<subcircuit circuitJson={...}>` import, the feed's `is_covered_with_solder_mask` changes from `true` to `false`.

Both regression tests use `test.failing`, so CI passes while verifying that the solder-mask import bug is still reproducible. The fix in #4973 restores regular `test` calls. The antenna test captures one snapshot of the imported board before asserting that its feed must remain masked. The secondary regression uses numeric assertions for all six pad shapes on both layers, positive/zero/negative margins, omitted defaults, and saved-JSON immutability. It exposes ten lost coverage flags and thirty dropped margins; polygon pads preserve the settings.

Validation: `bun test tests/repros/repro-antenna-mask-round-trip.test.tsx tests/repros/repro-smtpad-mask-round-trip.test.tsx` passes both expected-failure tests (Bun 1.3.3). Gerber validation with `circuit-json-to-gerber@0.0.121` confirms the antenna changes from zero mask openings to one unintended opening.

Fix: #4973, the next layer in native GitHub stack #4976.

The single snapshot shows the imported antenna. Hatching marks the copper keepout; the red feed square is the unintended exposed copper.

![Imported antenna with unintended feed exposure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/2b147b1341fe53933a32eebf9e436dcdae4308c8/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-antenna-mask-round-trip-imported-board-pcb.snap.svg)

Formatting and diff checks pass.

body:
Render assembly explosion stages and movements into the circuit database, so ordinary Circuit JSON contains a complete playback program and viewers can move all parts targeted by a stage without keeping the TSX tree.

`AssemblyExplosionStage` and `AssemblyExplosionMove` follow core's render lifecycle. `CadExplosionStageRender` allocates database-owned stage IDs after CAD settles; `CadExplosionRender` resolves membership, order, targets and world-space translation vectors. Separate phases support forward stage references. Initial/update/removal hooks keep IDs stable, refresh dependent membership and delete owned moves when a stage is removed. `getCircuitJson()` remains the normal database getter. Invalid references and membership cycles fail during rendering.

`targetRef`/`targetRefs` can name another explosion stage: its members move together, preserving earlier displacement without replaying its instructions. `getCircuitJsonAssemblyExplosion()` validates the serialized program and supports sequential partial progress and backward scrubbing without mutating assembled geometry. Overlapping targets move once per instruction; derived pose exports omit instructions to prevent double application.

Four new annotated snapshot sheets cover **20 views**, rendered natively from the original serialized program through [circuit-json-to-gltf #274](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/274):

- [Round trip, sequential partial progress, whole-stage overlap and backward scrubbing](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/feat/serialize-assembly-explosions/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-explosion-json-round-trip-annotated.snap.png): six views.
- [Upright, inverted and tilted mounting frames](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/feat/serialize-assembly-explosions/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-explosion-json-frame-annotated.snap.png): four views.
- [Retargeting, removal and restoration through render phases](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/feat/serialize-assembly-explosions/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-explosion-render-lifecycle-annotated.snap.png): four views.
- Real RP2040/NEMA17 assembly: assembled, all four stages and halfway through bolt removal. The cover and entire bolt stage lift together first, then the bolts, motor and spacers separate. The captions show actual TSX in a bundled monospace font. Pinned model bytes make the snapshots independent of network downloads.

![Real RP2040 assembly: every stage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/feat/serialize-assembly-explosions/tests/assembly/__snapshots__/assembly-explosion-rp2040-stages-annotated.snap.png)

Uses published `circuit-json@^0.0.539` from merged [circuit-json #937](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/937) and `circuit-json-to-gltf@^0.0.159` from merged [exporter #274](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/274). There are no preview package dependencies. The dependency gate remains enabled and passes. Downstream viewer: [3d-viewer #1082](https://github.com/tscircuit/3d-viewer/pull/1082).

The explicit `serializeAssemblyExplosion(roots, assembledGeometry)` adapter shares the resolver for already-rendered trees from older core releases; normal rendering does not call it. The real RP2040 fixture retains its pinned 0.0.2199 PCB renderer and copper-preservation guards because newer PCB rendering trips its ground-pour guard. Its custom assembly TSX, original board attribution, JSON and model hashes are checked in. The snapshot retains 300 routed traces, 303 vias and 117 CAD components; its 201 pre-existing schema rejections are documented and unchanged.

Validation with the published exporter: all **94 assembly tests pass**, including all four annotated snapshot sheets without updates. Typecheck, dependency checks, class exports, package build and distribution smoke tests pass. Another 29 related tests pass; seven local PCB-flex SVG snapshot failures reproduce with identical pixel differences on unchanged `main` using exporter `0.0.158`. No unrelated baselines were changed. The real-board TSX re-export preserves all 5,109 assembled records exactly. The branch includes `main` through `7c67bf75a` (0.0.2233); all ten CI test groups, typecheck, dependency checks, formatting, class exports, preview build and distribution smoke tests pass at `f9fc5c4a3`. The root README is unchanged.

CAD/reference-surface translations only; PCB/cable-containing targets and rotations remain unsupported. Pose sampling supports stage snapshots and scrubbing, not embedded GLTF animation tracks. No swept-collision claim.

title: refactor: resolve component-specific Footprinter definitions in core
description: Core and Footprinter could both generate polarity artwork for LEDs, producing duplicate symbols. Bare LED package sizes also selected resistor definitions. Resolve each components effective footprint and let Footprinter generate the requested artwork. Use published Footprinter 0.0.450 and its resolvePassiveFootprintDefinition API to select capacitor and diode families while retaining explicit families, dimensions, units, and modifiers. Chip.resolveFootprint() requests _nonpolarized only for diodeLED packages that generate automatic electrical polarity artwork. Ordinary chip footprints such as soic8, qfn32, and dip8 retain their definitions. Explicit polarity modifiers are preserved. Capacitor.getFootprinterString() owns capacitor family selection, polarity options, and terminal mapping. PCB and CAD use the same definition. Diodes and LEDs share diode-specific footprint and port helpers under libutilsfootprints. Component class files retain their class export; a CI regression rejects additional runtime exports in normal component class files. Read parameters directly from Footprinter instead of maintaining a duplicate Zod schema. Convert authored pin options at the terminal-mapping boundary, preserving label conflict checks and distinct numeric 1  2 terminals. Keep NormalComponent generic and authored props immutable. Remove cores duplicate LEDcapacitor fabrication generators while preserving importedcustom artwork. For example, a polarized capacitor using 0805 resolves to cap0805_polarized; an 0805 LED resolves to diode0805; a generic chip using sod123 resolves to sod123_nonpolarized, while soic8 remains soic8.
body:
Core and Footprinter could both generate polarity artwork for LEDs, producing duplicate symbols. Bare LED package sizes also selected resistor definitions. Resolve each component's effective footprint and let Footprinter generate the requested artwork.

- Use published Footprinter **0.0.450** and its `resolvePassiveFootprintDefinition` API to select capacitor and diode families while retaining explicit families, dimensions, units, and modifiers.
- `Chip.resolveFootprint()` requests `_nonpolarized` only for diode/LED packages that generate automatic electrical polarity artwork. Ordinary chip footprints such as `soic8`, `qfn32`, and `dip8` retain their definitions. Explicit polarity modifiers are preserved.
- `Capacitor.getFootprinterString()` owns capacitor family selection, polarity options, and terminal mapping. PCB and CAD use the same definition.
- Diodes and LEDs share diode-specific footprint and port helpers under `lib/utils/footprints/`. Component class files retain their class export; a CI regression rejects additional runtime exports in normal component class files.
- Read parameters directly from Footprinter instead of maintaining a duplicate Zod schema. Convert authored pin options at the terminal-mapping boundary, preserving label conflict checks and distinct numeric `1 | 2` terminals.
- Keep NormalComponent generic and authored props immutable. Remove core's duplicate LED/capacitor fabrication generators while preserving imported/custom artwork.

For example, a polarized capacitor using `0805` resolves to `cap0805_polarized`; an `0805` LED resolves to `diode0805`; a generic chip using `sod123` resolves to `sod123_nonpolarized`, while `soic8` remains `soic8`.

Validation:
- 38 focused tests across 33 files pass, covering footprint resolution, PCB/CAD parity, diode/LED behavior, capacitor polarity, terminal conflicts, geometry, and class exports.
- TypeScript check, package build, distribution smoke tests, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

title: Choose breakout exit edges per connection
description: Fixes breakout routing by allowing each connection to choose its exit edge based on the shortest path to its destination, improving routing efficiency and reducing manual breakout points.
body:
## Problem

A `<breakout>` solved on its own (the common case: no other automatic breakout shares its connections) sent **every** exit through one edge. `getSingleRegionPreferredEdge` added up the distance from all external destinations to each edge and picked the lowest total. `busFanoutDirections` never reached the implicit breakout point step either.

On an AM3352 + DDR3L board, all 91 SoC exits left through the bottom edge (toward the DDR), including LCD nets bound for an HDMI bridge on the right and USB nets bound for connectors on top. The workaround was 42 manual `<breakoutpoint>`s, which also grew the breakout box from 22.9mm to 27.9mm because padding is re-added around them.

## Fix

For a single-region breakout scope (multi-breakout scopes keep their facing-edge logic):

- **Edge per connection.** Each connection takes the edge that minimizes its path: a straight escape from the pin to the edge, then a straight run from that exit to its nearest destination.
- **Pairs and buses stay together.** Differential pairs and buses move as a unit.
- **Edge-first `busFanoutDirections` are honored.** A value like `leftside_bottom` pins the bus to that edge and band. Legacy NinePointAnchor names stay destination-guided, as documented.
- **Edges have capacity.** When an edge is over its estimated capacity, the units that lose least by moving go to edges with room.
- **The solver runs once per edge group.** Groups sharing an edge are slid apart rigidly, which preserves order, spacing and layer stagger. The winding solver rejects bounds that don't contain every pin, so bands are applied by shifting, not by narrowing bounds.
- **Parts inside the bounds count as destinations.** Ports of parts placed inside the breakout's bounds but not in it (e.g. a crystal next to an SoC) used to be ignored.
- **New warning.** A `busFanoutDirections` key that names no bus emits `source_property_ignored_warning`.

When every connection picks the same edge and no band applies, the solver input is unchanged.

## Tests

- `single-breakout-per-connection-edges1`: BGA with destinations left, right and bottom gets exits on all three edges. Before this change all seven went out the bottom.
- `single-breakout-per-connection-edges2`: `busFanoutDirections={{ DATA: "leftside_bottom" }}` puts DATA on the lower third of the left edge, even though its destinations are on the right.
- `single-breakout-per-connection-edges3`: an edge too small for 12 single-layer exits spills some to neighbouring edges instead of failing.
- `single-breakout-per-connection-edges4`: a part inside the breakout's bounds gets an exit facing it.
- `breakout-insufficient-fanout-space-error`: that tight QFN's 24 exits now split across two edges, so breakout points are solvable and the error surfaces in the fanout escape. The message assertions are unchanged. The "no breakout points" assertion now checks "no unresolved points at the origin", which is its stated intent.
- Snapshots updated: `breakout-sot23-regulator-power-rail` and `fanout-soic8-sensor-to-i2c-header` (exits face their destinations, fewer vias), and `breakout-qfp16-with-header-and-passives`.
- `repro-shared-capacitor-breakout-handoff` will change: its `RETURN: "rightside_center"` is now honored at breakout-point placement. Locally this snapshot already differs because of text rendering, so it wasn't regenerated here.

On the AM3352 board, removing the 42 manual breakout points now gives sensible exits on all four SoC edges:
- DDR on the bottom.
- LCD, GPMC and the crystal on the right.
- PMIC on the left.
- USB on top and right.

The SoC fanout then escapes 195 of 202, against 194 with the manual points. The remaining failures come from FanoutSolver's escape search, not from this step.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix: via-in-pad no longer crashes the autorouter
description: Fixes autorouting failure when placing a via inside a same-net SMT pad, preventing crashes in the autorouter.
body:
## Problem

Placing a `<via>` inside a same-net SMT pad (BGA via-in-pad) made the default autorouter crash and leave the trace unrouted:

```
TopologyMergingSolver: output nodes "obstacle-pcb_component_0-…:top…" and "cmn_13" have an unresolved inter-group overlap on a shared layer
```

`getObstaclesFromCircuitJson` emitted the pad and the via as two separate obstacles that overlap on the pad's layer. This came from a user's AM3352 six-layer board, which had 322 vias in pads. They worked around it by rewriting the SRJ obstacles in an `autorouting:start` hook.

## Fix

`separateViaInPadObstacles` runs at the end of `getObstaclesFromCircuitJson`. A plain (non-assignable) via that sits entirely inside a same-net SMT pad drops the pad's layer(s) from its obstacle. On that layer the via adds no copper beyond the pad. Both obstacles keep their real geometry, and they no longer overlap on a shared layer.

I first tried merging the via into the pad obstacle, as the user's workaround does, and dropped it. Extending a pad onto every layer over-blocks the inner layers. `repro-am62l-direct-decoupling-fanout` went from pass to fail ("only 112 of 135 connections could escape").

## Tests

- `repro-bga-via-in-pad-routing1`: 6x6 0.8mm BGA with a via in the pad of an inner ball. The pad and via obstacles don't share a layer, and the trace routes with no autorouting error. Crashes on main.
- `repro-bga-via-in-pad-routing2`: same BGA with 0.6mm pads, so no trace fits between balls on top. The route leaves through the via on an inner layer, with no second via added at the pad. Crashes on main.

Local checks: `tsc --noEmit` is clean, and `repro-am62l-direct-decoupling-fanout` passes. I ran the via/fanout/breakout/`tests/utils/autorouting` files (~94). 20 of them fail locally, but they fail identically on unmodified main, and all are `toMatchPcbSnapshot` mismatches from my local environment.

## Not in this PR

- `@tscircuit/checks` doesn't treat a via in the pad as connecting the trace to the pad. A route that starts on an inner layer at a pad with an in-pad via can be flagged `missing a connection to SMD pad`.
- There's no first-class way for a footprint or pad to declare its own vias. Vias are placed by absolute coordinates.

Also bumps `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` to 0.0.1013, which includes the matching router-side fix (tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3333): the topology merging solver no longer throws when a via sits inside a same-net BGA pad.

title: Measure test point label obstacles once per layer
description: Reduces the time taken to measure obstacles for test point labels by measuring each layers obstacles once instead of for each test point, resulting in significant performance improvements.
body:
Follow-up to #4982. `placeTestPointSilkscreenLabels` rebuilt the bounds of every pad, hole, via and silkscreen element on the layer for each generated test point, so labeling was O(test points × obstacles).

Measured with the PD power supply board from the real-board test fixture, also tiled 4× and 16× side by side:

| Board | Obstacles | 200 test points before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Real board | 793 | 61 ms | 4 ms |
| 4× | 3,172 | 211 ms | 6 ms |
| 16× | 12,688 | 812 ms | ~20 ms |

Each layer's obstacles are now measured once, and each placed label's bounds (still measured with `getPcbElementBounds`) is added to its layer's list, so later labels avoid it as before. The remaining per-candidate overlap checks are cheap at this scale.

Placements are unchanged. Running the previous and new versions on 50 and 400 test points across top and bottom layers produced identical label text, layer and position for every label, including the many labels that moved off their default position. The test-point tests pass and `tsc --noEmit` passes.

title: Label generated test points on silkscreen
description: Adds silkscreen labels for generated test points in autorouting, ensuring they are properly named and positioned without overlapping other elements.
body:
Generated test points (`<autoroutingphase reroute addTestPoints />`) had no silkscreen. They're materialized as circuit JSON after routing, not through the `TestPoint` class, so they never got the reference label a regular `<testpoint />` has.

**Labels** (`lib/utils/autorouting/place-test-point-silkscreen-labels.ts`)
- **Text:** the probed net's name, else the trace's `name`, else `TP_1`, `TP_2`, … Names already used by a component or another label are skipped. Components keep their `TP_AUTO_<phase>_<n>` names.
- **Style:** matches a regular test point's label (`tscircuit2024`, font size 0.4, center 0.5 mm from the pad edge) and uses the pad's layer, so bottom test points get bottom silkscreen.
- **Placement:** an 8-position search around the pad (above, below, right, left, then diagonals). It keeps the first position that stays inside the board and doesn't overlap pads, holes, vias or silkscreen on that layer, including labels placed earlier in the same pass. It falls back to above.

**Fix: test points on net-routed connections**

A routed connection through a named net resolves to a `source_net` id, which failed with `Test point … has no source connection`. `Group` now resolves such a route to one of that net's own `source_trace`s, so `sourceTraceId` is always a source trace. The test point joins the net through it, and its label reads the net name from that trace.

**Tests**
- New `autoroutingphase-test-points-silkscreen-names`: labels are `VSENSE` (net), `SCL` (trace name) and `TP_1` (unnamed), and the `VSENSE` test point is connected to the net.
- New `autoroutingphase-test-points-silkscreen-placement`: with silkscreen text occupying the default spot, the label moves below the pad.
- The two existing test-point PCB snapshots now include their `TP_1` labels.
- The PD power supply real-board test still adds no DRC findings.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes. Locally, across the 34 autorouting-phase and test-point test files, 11 unrelated tests fail with and without this change (same set).

title: Let manufacturerPartNumber and supplierPartNumbers pin standard connectors
description: Allows standard connectors to pin specific parts by using manufacturerPartNumber and supplierPartNumbers, preventing unintended changes in part selection over time.
body:
Standard connectors (`<connector standard="usb_c" />` and the JST standards) always called the parts engine's `findPart` to choose a part. For `usb_c`, the JLC parts engine ranks candidates by stock and ignores `manufacturer_part_number`. So the same code can resolve to a different footprint over time, and setting `manufacturerPartNumber` or `supplierPartNumbers` didn't pin it. svg.tscircuit.com hit this: its `standard="usb_c"` snapshot test changed from a through-hole part to JLCPCB C2765186 (`TYPE-C 16PIN 2MD(073)`) with no code change, so it is skipped in tscircuit/svg.tscircuit.com#2765 for now.

**Change** (`Connector.doInitialFetchPartFootprint`)
- **`supplierPartNumbers` set:** fetch those parts and skip `findPart`. The prop's numbers stay on the source component, including on failure.
- **Only `manufacturerPartNumber` set:** skip `findPart` and call `fetchPartCircuitJson({ manufacturerPartNumber })`, which the JLC parts engine resolves by exact MPN match. `supplier_part_numbers` is left unset rather than filled with stock-ranked candidates that may be a different part.
- **Neither set:** unchanged, still searches with `findPart`.

**Tests**
- New `connector-usbc-pinned-supplier-part.test.tsx`: `findPart` is never called, and only the pinned part is fetched.
- New `connector-usbc-pinned-mpn.test.tsx`: `findPart` is never called, and exactly one MPN-only fetch is made.
- Both fail without the fix.
- `parts-engine-fetch-circuit-json-circuit-json-not-found.test.tsx` encoded the old order (findPart's part first, then MPN). It now expects the single MPN fetch and no supplier numbers.
- `connector-usbc-schematic-text-position.test.tsx`'s mock now also answers its part's MPN (`HRO-TYPE-C-31-M-12`); its snapshot is unchanged.
- Locally, across the 60 connector/parts-engine test files: 54 pass, 8 fail with and without this change (identical sets, environment-related). `tsc --noEmit` passes.

Once released, svg.tscircuit.com can re-enable its test, which already sets `manufacturerPartNumber="TYPE-C 16PIN 2MD(073)"`.

title: Resolve drawing dimensions from jscad geometry instead of circuit-json-to-gltf
description: Changes the method of resolving drawing dimensions by using jscad geometry directly instead of relying on circuit-json-to-gltf, reducing bundle size and improving performance.
body:
Core imported `circuit-json-to-gltf` at runtime only to place assembly drawing dimensions. It built the selected parts in 3D, exported a GLB and reloaded it with poppygl. That pulled the whole 3D stack, including occt-import-js's 7.6 MB WASM and native resvg, into every bundle of core. tscircuit/eval#5427 needed webworker build workarounds because of it, and the worker grew from ~18 MB to ~30 MB.

This change builds the same geometry directly as poppygl draw calls with jscad and matrix math. `circuit-json-to-gltf` becomes a dev dependency only (tests still render drawing snapshots with it) and is removed from `peerDependencies`.

**New: `lib/utils/assembly-drawing/geometry/get-drawing-draw-calls.ts`**
- **Board:** the outline (or rectangle) extruded through its thickness, with hole loops using circuit-json-to-gltf's 24/8-segment tessellation. The profile is built from its loops rather than with jscad booleans, which snap vertices by ~1e-4 mm. Vertices stay board-relative like the exporter's mesh. On the hole-dimension circuit, bounds and all 152 vertices match the previous pipeline exactly.
- **`model_jscad` parts:** the raw jscad triangles plus one model matrix that reproduces the exporter's placement in order: loader axis swap, `model_unit_to_mm_scale_factor`, `model_board_normal_direction`, origin (`model_origin_position`, including its default-loader-transform mapping, or inferred `model_origin_alignment`), `model_object_fit` against `size`, CAD rotation (bottom-layer default flip) and position, then the glTF handedness flip.
- **Named feature outlines (`edgeRef`):** they reuse the part's model matrix instead of normalizing into the exporter's fitted bounding box and round-tripping through GLB.

Camera fitting, section cuts and bounds still use poppygl (`buildCamera`, `createOutlineSection`, `computeWorldAABB`); only the source of the draw calls changed.

**Not supported in dimensioned views (clear error instead)**
- Imported model files (STL/OBJ/GLB/glTF/STEP) and footprinter-generated models. These need loaders that core shouldn't bundle.
- Folded boards (`pcb_bend`). Previously only board and hole references rejected these.
- Hole shapes other than round or rectangular.

`tests/assembly/assembly-drawing-dimension-imported-model.test.tsx` now expects a dimensioned view of a part with `model_glb_url` to reject with that error (its snapshot is removed). Imported-model support can come later, e.g. through an optional mesh loader in `platformConfig`.

**Verification**
- `tests/assembly`: 87 pass, 0 fail. All other assembly-drawing snapshots are unchanged, so dimension positions and the fitted `scale` match.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes. The built dist has no runtime import of circuit-json-to-gltf.
- tscircuit/eval built against this core, with eval's original webworker config and the released circuit-json-to-gltf: the worker builds with no resvg plugin or externals, is 18.8 MB with no occt or resvg code, and all 4 Playwright browser tests pass.

The actual astra/pd-power-supply board is pinned at release 57387f49-bd91-4277-8a82-706b1575c5ed. SDA and OUTPUT_EN use top-accessible branches of the same nets; the 0.2 mm clearance, 2.54 mm probe spacing and 1 mm detour limit are unchanged. The full-board snapshot uses standard PCB colors, shows footprint pads and silkscreen, and labels the new pads in magenta. Copper pours are hidden only in the image.

Prototype scope: one final phase, outer-layer pads, bounded local detours, and rejection of fixed routes or impossible requests. Probe coordinates remain in board space; fixture mechanics and transforms are the following step.

The test-point phase runs inside the existing autorouting async effect using a GenericLocalAutorouter adapter. It shares the normal awaited complete/error/progress handling and stop cleanup, and yields between target searches (individual target searches remain synchronous). Regression tests cover asynchronous yielding, stopping without completion, failed placement without partial output, and circuit-level progress forwarding.

title: Fix false power-pin warnings for passive components
description: Fixes false power-pin warnings for passive components by exempting fully passive components from power-pin checks.
body:
## Motivation

The [Macro Six USB-C board](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/macro-six-usbc) board uses an EC11E18244AU mechanical encoder for volume control. Its imported component uses <chip>, but it has no power-supply pin: it works through passive contacts. All seven pins are explicitly marked passive and connected to the board’s signal or ground nets.

The power-pin checker currently treats this component like a powered chip and reports ENC1 has no pin with requires_power=true, despite those passive attributes. This creates a misleading warning for a component that cannot truthfully declare a power pin.

This fixes the behaviour reproduced in #500 by skipping the power-pin warning when every connectable pin is explicitly passive. Components with non-passive or unspecified pins remain checked.

## Before and after

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ENC1 reports `has no pin with requires_power=true`. | ENC1 produces no power-pin warning. |
| Passive pin markings do not prevent this warning. | Fully passive components are exempt; components with non-passive or unspecified pins are still checked. |

## Motivation

On [Macro Six USB-C board](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/macro-six-usbc) macro keyboard shows a missing-power-pin warning for its volume encoder, even though this mechanical component does not need a power pin. Its pins are already marked passive, but the checker still expects power because the imported encoder uses <chip>.

The reproduction uses ENC1’s real connections: A → ENC_A, B → ENC_B, D → ENC_PUSH, and C/E/pin6/pin7 → GND. It verifies that all seven exported pins are passive and connected, then captures the incorrect warning.

title: Warn about isolated copper pour islands in routing DRC

body:
Net-assigned copper pour islands currently pass routing DRC when they have no physical path to a same-net pad or via. Add `checkCopperPourIslands` to the public API and `runAllRoutingChecks`, using the existing physical copper connectivity graph. Contacts respect layers, BRep holes, trace copper, and plated barrels; a shared net name alone cannot connect islands.

Emit advisory `pcb_copper_pour_isolated_warning` records carrying original pour/net references, layer, and board-world center. Messages use readable net names and approximate coordinates. Unassigned decorative copper is ignored. The shared graph also handles interpolated trace widths and wire-to-via segments to avoid false island reports.

Uses `circuit-json@0.0.537`, which provides the dedicated warning schema from merged https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/933. Uses the published npm package; no schema preview dependency or override remains.

On the [reported AM3352 six-layer board](https://am3352-six-layer-routing-proof.seveibar.chatgpt.site/#file=am3352.circuit.json), the check reports 141 GND islands (17 bottom, 105 inner1, 19 inner4), plus 113 power-net islands. Include a reduced original GND BRep fixture.

The test runs the detector on all 323 pours and renders every original geometry record in its original location. Only pre-existing unrelated warning records are excluded from the render.

Native highlighting from merged https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/887 provides exact pour boundaries, BRep holes and arcs, a location ring, and hover messages, gated by `shouldDrawWarnings` and the selected layer. Uses published `circuit-to-svg@0.0.454` without a Git pin or trusted install script.

title: Avoid quadratic net-member scans when adding connections
description: Reduces the time complexity of adding connections by utilizing a reverse membership index, resulting in significantly faster performance for large datasets.
body:
Repeated imported copper aliases currently scan a growing net array for every ID. Use the reverse membership index already maintained by the constructor and net merges to decide whether an ID needs appending, preserving member order and net aliases.

The included shared-power-net benchmark (4,096 members repeated across 128 obstacles) runs in ABBA order: baseline 1,824 / 1,694 ms versus candidate 23.9 / 22.0 ms, approximately 77× faster, with identical output hashes. This is a focused benchmark, not a full-router speedup claim. The motherboard full-route trial also preserves output and iteration count; end-to-end paired validation is ongoing in the integration work.

Validation: all 28 tests pass (14,096 assertions), TypeScript and build pass. The new test compares 4,000 incremental operations against a frozen original implementation, including initial overlapping membership and repeated merges. Run `bun benchmarks/add-connections.ts` to reproduce the focused comparison.

title: fix: export PnP from authored footprint origin
description: Fixes the pick-and-place coordinate to use the authored footprint origin instead of the geometric center, improving alignment for asymmetric footprints.
body:
## Summary

Use `pcb_component.footprint_origin` as the pick-and-place coordinate when it is available, with `pcb_component.center` retained as the fallback for older Circuit JSON.

This is stacked on the TSX repro-only PR:

- #26

## Why

`center` is the geometric bounds center and can be displaced by asymmetric footprint geometry such as an offset mechanical cutout. `footprint_origin` is the authored component origin that core already preserves through placement transforms and uses for CAD placement.

The fix is generic: it contains no sensor, cutout, package, or coordinate special cases.

## Visual snapshot change

The same tscircuit TSX fixture from #26 is rendered through core. The stacked diff updates the visual SVG so the exported PnP target moves from `(0, -0.775)` to `(0, 0.2)`. The red target now aligns with the green footprint-origin / pin-grid marker.

The explicit row assertion changes at the same time:

```diff
- mid_y: -0.775
+ mid_y: 0.2
```

Existing fixtures without `footprint_origin` continue using `center`, exercising the compatibility fallback.

## Verification

- `bun test` (53 passing)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: test: reproduce asymmetric footprint PnP offset
description: Reproduces a bug where the PnP export incorrectly uses the bounds center instead of the footprint origin for asymmetric footprints, adding a test fixture and SVG snapshot to illustrate the issue.
body:
## Problem

For an asymmetric footprint, `pcb_component.center` is the geometric bounds center while `pcb_component.footprint_origin` is the authored assembly origin. The current PnP export uses the bounds center, so an offset mechanical cutout can shift the manufactured placement away from the pin grid.

The TSX fixture reproduces the sensor geometry using a real tscircuit `<chip>`, `<footprint>`, 16 `<platedhole>` elements, and an offset `<cutout>`. `Circuit.renderUntilSettled()` generates the Circuit JSON; the test does not hand-author component coordinates.

The generated values make the issue explicit:

- bounds center: `(0, -0.775)`
- footprint origin / pin-grid center: `(0, 0.2)`
- current exported PnP position: `(0, -0.775)`

## Visual reproduction

The committed SVG snapshot renders the generated footprint and overlays the coordinate produced by this package:

- green diamond: authored footprint origin / pin-grid center
- red target: exported PnP position

In this repro, the red target is visibly below the green origin:

`tests/__snapshots__/asymmetric-footprint-origin.snap.svg`

## Scope

This is a repro-only PR. It adds a focused TSX fixture, a visual SVG snapshot, and an explicit row assertion for the current incorrect output; it does not change production code.

The development `circuit-json` dependency is updated from `0.0.520` to `0.0.534` so the existing `footprint_origin` field is typed, and `tscircuit` is added as a development dependency to render the fixture from TSX.

The fix is submitted as a separate PR stacked on this branch.

## Verification

- `bun test` (53 passing)
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run build`

title: Report unlisted requested parts as unknown without failing inventory refresh
description: Classifies validated empty exact searches as unknown inventory in the per-part report, preventing failures in inventory refresh for unlisted part numbers.
body:
JLCPCB returns HTTP 200 with componentPageInfo.total=0 and list=null for some unlisted exact part numbers. The first production requested-inventory run successfully refreshed 147 parts, including C7519, but failed overall on this normal empty result for C6998930.

Classify validated empty exact searches as unknown inventory in the per-part report. Do not invent zero stock or advance the verification timestamp. HTTP failures, malformed nonempty responses, invalid stock, and duplicate matches remain pipeline failures. This keeps unknown parts observable without causing every hourly run to fail because a user searched for an unlisted ID.

Validation: four requested-stock tests (27 assertions), including the observed null-list response, pass; root and Worker TypeScript checks pass.

title: Keep BOM-requested parts fresh independently of category crawl coverage
description: Registers exact BOM lookups for hourly refresh in a separate job, ensuring that stocked parts are updated independently of category crawls or catalog imports.
body:
Exact BOM lookups hid stocked parts after their live observations expired: C7519 returned no result while JLCPCB reported roughly 35,900 units. Its previous live observation was about two weeks old.

Register exact numeric/C-prefixed searches for hourly refresh in a separate job that cannot be blocked by long category crawls or catalog imports. Refresh recently requested parts directly from JLCPCB, retain verified metadata across nightly catalog replacement, and update stock in existing category tables. Exact responses bypass cached empty results, preserve unknown stock as null and confirmed zero as zero, and expose a verification timestamp. Verified exact stock expires after six hours without a successful refresh. First-time misses enroll for the next scheduled refresh rather than blocking the request on JLCPCB.

The bounded refresh processes the oldest attempts first, records errors without inventing zero stock, uploads a per-part report, and fails visibly when supplier lookups fail. Manual backfills avoid the broad crawler's shared staging table. See docs/requested-inventory.md for rollout and capacity limits.

Validation:
- Full Bun suite: 453 passed, 1 Worker-only test skipped; that integration test passes under Vitest/Workers.
- Existing Worker suite: 183 passed; new exact lookup/registration/expiry integration test passed separately.
- Root and Worker TypeScript checks and formatting passed.
- Applied the migration, refreshed all 124 placements / 57 unique JLCPCB part numbers from release bf3e0595-da86-4ee0-a9a0-ba6ee6c39825, and deployed the Worker.
- All 57 public API results match fresh supplier checks: 56 stocked parts, and genuine zero stock for U_PD / C970725 (CH224K). C7519 reports 35,901 at verification; C5981428, previously missing, reports 547.

Merging activates priority refreshes in the existing hourly inventory workflow. Saved circuit warnings still require a rebuild; this PR does not modify the board design.

body:
Microcontroller search now supports CAN, SPI, I²C, UART, and USB Host filters, combined with AND matching. USB Host uses an exact-part manufacturer evidence ledger covering the entire production snapshot: 9,763 listings and 9,745 distinct manufacturer ordering codes, including out-of-stock parts.

| USB host decision | Listings |
| --- | ---: |
| Confirmed host | 2,137 |
| Confirmed no host | 7,559 |
| Unresolved | 67 |

Three GPT-6.1 Terra reviewers checked manufacturer documents, with source recovery and cross-checks for package, silicon, ordering, and document-revision differences. Each confirmed decision records its source, document, evidence and matching method; unresolved entries record specific missing or conflicting evidence. The 67 unresolved listings may include additional hosts, so this does not claim every host is proven. Unknowns remain NULL and match neither Yes nor No.

The audit preserves package exceptions such as PSoC 6 and SAM variants, and uses current manufacturer evidence where older USB device-only wording was incomplete. Native controllers requiring an external PHY are included; external programmers, USB hubs and Type-C power roles do not establish host support.

Migration 0018 adds and backfills the host column using exact order codes, preserves stock and unrelated data, and sets USB support for confirmed hosts. Derived-table rebuilds use the same ledger and preserve reviewed unknowns despite conflicting supplier attributes. The full-catalog read-only export and its hash are recorded in the ledger.

[Audit methodology, provenance, limitations and regeneration instructions](https://github.com/tscircuit/jlcsearch/blob/feat/mcu-interface-filters/docs/microcontroller-usb-host-audit.md).

Validation: all 450 tests pass; root and worker type checks pass; format check passes. Tests execute the actual migration against all 9,763 catalog rows and cover package/revision regressions, stock preservation, unknown handling and combined filters.

title: Fix missing USB microcontrollers by importing the current MCU category
description: Fixes the issue where the USB microcontroller list does not include current MCU categories, ensuring proper recognition and classification of USB-enabled microcontrollers in the database.
body:
The reported `/microcontrollers/list?package=&has_usb=true&core=&flash_min=&ram_min=` currently returns just one part. The live component catalog contains STM32F103C8T6 and other MCUs under `Microcontrollers (MCU/MPU/SOC)`, but the derived-table importer only recognizes the legacy category name and vendor-specific categories. Those rows never reach the existing USB audit overrides.

Accept the current category alongside all legacy categories, and include `microcontroller` in the merge-triggered derived-table sync so production is rebuilt after merge. Existing USB classifications are preserved.

Validation: 18 importer and USB-audit tests pass. The new source-db-v2 regression covers current/legacy categories, audited USB and non-USB parts, and exclusion of unrelated categories; it fails without the category fix. Formatting and `git diff --check` pass. Tests used a workspace TMPDIR because the host's /tmp quota prevented SQLite writes.

Production results will update after merge and successful completion of Build and Sync D1.

title: Bump core to 0.0.2222 and props to 0.0.714 for addTestPoints
description: Bumps tscircuitcore to 0.0.2222 and tscircuitprops to 0.0.714 to support autoroutingphase reroute addTestPoints  and ensure proper handling of test points in the circuit evaluation process.
body:
Bumps `@tscircuit/core` to 0.0.2222 and `@tscircuit/props` to 0.0.714 so the bundled evaluator supports `<autoroutingphase reroute addTestPoints />` from tscircuit/core#4974. Props 0.0.714 is required: older props schemas silently strip `addTestPoints` and the `testPoint*` options. This is needed for the docs preview in tscircuit/docs#970, via svg.tscircuit.com.

- Runs `copy-core-versions` to sync the rest of core's dependency versions. I left out `@tscircuit/test-point-rerouter`: core bundles it into its dist, so eval doesn't need it.
- **No webworker build changes.** Core 0.0.2202–0.0.2221 imported `circuit-json-to-gltf` for assembly drawing dimensions, which pulled resvg, occt-import-js (with a 10 MB inlined WASM) and Node built-ins into the worker and broke `build:webworker`. That's also why the automated updates since #5391 failed. tscircuit/core#4977 (released in 0.0.2222) removed that runtime import, so `tsup-webworker.config.ts` is unchanged from main.
- Adds `tests/features/autoroutingphase-test-points.test.tsx`, which runs `addTestPoints` through `CircuitRunner` and expects two `TP_AUTO_*` pads.
- Updates two KiCad import snapshots. The only change is the rotation of some imported silkscreen text; pad, trace, via and hole geometry is unchanged. Both pass on main's deps, so this comes from core changes since 0.0.2202 (first seen in the automated update for core 0.0.2203, #5391).

Local: `bun run build`, `tsc --noEmit`, the full `bun test tests` (171 pass, 0 fail) and all 4 Playwright browser tests pass. `dist/webworker/entrypoint.js` is 18.8 MB (0.0.1660: 18.2 MB) and contains no resvg, occt-import-js or svg-to-png code.

body:
The responsive toolbar change in #5945 added `overflow-x: auto` to the preview tab strip. CSS then computes the other axis to `auto`, exposing a vertical scrollbar because the More views button extends the 36px strip's scroll height to 38px.

Explicitly set `overflow-y: hidden` on this tab strip, preserving horizontal scrolling for narrow previews. Regenerate the bundled CSS (the only generated change is the new overflow-y utility).

Validation: Chromium layout reproduction using the actual component classes and generated stylesheet at 620px and 200px widths confirmed vertical overflow changes from auto to hidden and horizontal scrolling still works at 200px. Four existing UI tests passed: extra-runframe-tabs-ui, extra-runframe-tabs-ui2, host-window-controls, and responsive-file-selector-ui. Biome formatting and git diff --check passed.

Downstream: merging triggers the existing npm publish workflow, which dispatches @tscircuit/runframe dependency updates to cli and tscircuit.com. Existing static sites that bundle a pinned RunFrame version must be rebuilt/redeployed after consuming the fixed release.

title: Skip dependency installation by default for standalone init
description: Changes the default behavior of standalone tsci init to skip dependency installation unless explicitly requested, improving usability in offline or restricted environments.
body:
Standalone `tsci init` installs `@types/react` and `tscircuit` even though the executable bundles its runtime dependencies. That invokes an external package manager and can fail on offline or restricted networks.

Default dependency installation to off when `TSCIRCUIT_STANDALONE=1`. Add `--install` to opt back in, preserve the standard CLI's automatic-install default, and keep `--no-install` working in both modes. Add six child-process regression cases covering the mode and flag combinations.

Release verification on macOS arm64, November 2:
- Downloaded and checksum-verified `manual-2026-11-02-41456715970`, binary version `0.0.3050`. The 72.9 MB archive took 19.53 seconds to download; the complete curl installer into an explicit user-owned destination took 22.40 seconds without administrator approval.
- The released binary's plain `tsci init board --yes` still attempted package installation. With npm reachable and `jscdn.tscircuit.com` blocked, it contacted that CDN, printed an installation failure, and then exited 0 with “Initialization complete.” Without a package manager on PATH it also printed an installation failure.
- The release's explicit `--no-install` path passed fully offline in 1.71 seconds. Offline PCB/3D preview generation also passed.
- This PR's real init implementation, using the production standalone environment flags, passed with and without Bun on PATH in 1.21 and 0.80 seconds. No proxy connections, installation warnings, node_modules, or lockfiles were produced.

Validation with Bun 1.4.4: all six regressions pass with external network access denied (48 assertions); type checking, repository formatting checks, and the production build pass. The init suite initially passed 13 tests with one existing skill-download timeout; that test passed on a targeted retry.

The remaining ordinary-install CDN path is `tscircuit@0.0.3052 → circuit-json-to-gltf@0.0.163 → jscad-electronics@0.0.242 → @tscircuit/jscad` via a direct tarball URL. A configured npm registry does not replace that URL. The newer npm releases exist, but the old `0.0.x` ranges continue selecting the CDN-dependent chain. https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/pull/6119 updates that path; https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5064 prevents dependency synchronization from restoring the old version. Their proposed consumer installation passes with the CDN blocked.

Release completion requires merging and publishing this CLI change, updating standalone's pinned CLI dependency, then building a new standalone release and rerunning plain init without `--no-install`. The current public standalone release does not include this fix. The reported one-hour delay was not reproduced; these timings do not establish which step consumed that hour.

title: Search all sources by default and add datasheet catalog search
description: Search all sources by default and add datasheet catalog search functionality, allowing users to query multiple sources concurrently and handle errors gracefully.
body:
An unqualified `tsci search LM358` currently queries only JLCPCB. Search all seven sources by default: KiCad, JLCPCB, Texas Instruments, DigiKey, Mouser, tscircuit registry packages, and datasheets. Explicit source flags restrict the search to the requested providers; `--lcsc` remains a JLCPCB alias.

Run selected searches concurrently with a shared ten-second request deadline. Preserve successful results when individual providers fail, report failures on stderr and in JSON `errors`, and exit unsuccessfully when every selected provider fails. Terminal output stays grouped by source, and JSON retains source identities and deterministic ordering.

Add `--datasheets` using the existing `/datasheets/list` API, configured endpoint, and platform fetch transport. Matching uses literal case-insensitive substrings, with exact matches first and up to ten results. No Fuse scoring is used for datasheets; existing KiCad matching is unchanged.

Deployments can configure one or more default providers using `TSCIRCUIT_DEFAULT_SEARCH_SOURCES=datasheets,jlcpcb`. With the setting absent, every provider is enabled. Explicit flags override configured defaults. No standalone checks, baked-file handling, new dependencies, or API changes are introduced.

Testing follows the repository's `getCliTestFixture().runCommand(...)` convention. The shared fixture invokes `bun run`, retaining its preload support. Four focused command-level tests cover combined JSON/terminal output, source selection and literal matching, partial/total failures, and configured defaults against baked HTTP inventories. External catalog responses are deterministic through the existing preload mechanism; commands still use the fixture's real registry server. The large in-process Commander/console-spy suite was removed.

Validation: 29 search/baked-server tests plus two existing auth command-fixture checks passed (31 total). TypeScript, formatting, and diff checks passed. Also captured a live `bun run cli/main.ts search LM358` to verify terminal output with multiple sources.

title: Default local autorouting to four threads
description: Default local Pipeline9 routing to four workers on Node and Bun 1.4.2, with fallback to one thread on older Bun versions to avoid unsupported worker startup.
body:
Default local Pipeline9 routing to four workers on Node and Bun >=1.4.2. The CLI's `getPlatformConfigWithCliDefaults` detects older Bun versions and defaults to one thread (inline routing), avoiding unsupported worker startup. This check belongs to the CLI platform-config loader; eval is unchanged.

Explicit project `autorouterThreads` settings still take precedence. Document the automatic default, runtime requirements, project configuration, worker creation/disposal, and file-build concurrency; link the guide from the README.

### Validation

- 17 targeted tests passed across version boundaries, Node detection, explicit overrides on old/new Bun, platform-map merging, runtime config command flows, and concurrent builds with function-valued config. These passed after moving fixture temporary files off a filesystem that rejected writes with EDQUOT.
- All 11 platform-default tests also passed under actual Bun 1.3.11.
- Cold-cache CLI builds of the recent 555 blinker with no thread override passed on both Bun 1.3.11 and Bun 1.4.4. The older runtime created zero routing workers; the newer runtime created and terminated four.
