title: fix: allow explicit native simulation process deadlines
description: Allows users to specify a per-process timeout for PCB SPICE simulations using the --solver-timeout-ms flag, enhancing control over simulation runtime.
body:
`tsci simulate` can now pass `--solver-timeout-ms <milliseconds>` to the native PCB SPICE adapter. A long FastHenry extraction can receive more runtime while retaining the same routed copper, mesh, convergence tolerances and numerical checks. Omission preserves the adapter's 900,000 ms per-process default. The flag applies independently to each FastHenry, FasterCap and ngspice request; it is not a total-run deadline.

Stacked on #5620 (native TSX command regression). Reject zero, negative, fractional, non-finite and timer-overflow values before loading the circuit, and reject the option for non-`pcb_spice` simulations. The upper bound avoids JavaScript timers turning an oversized deadline into an immediate timeout.

Example, after installing a release containing this change:
```sh
bunx --no-install tsci simulate simulations-next/run-ddr.circuit.tsx \
  --disable-parts-engine --solver-timeout-ms 1800000 \
  --output work/ddr-eye-99b75cf-30min
```
This command is documented, not executed in this investigation. The full AM3352 board still has no accepted refined matrix, waveform or eye.

Validation: the new native-TSX command tests pass for default/explicit/invalid/non-native options; the existing analog simulation test passes; return-current's native test is skipped by its existing environment gate. `bun run build` and formatting of all touched files pass; the built bundle exposes the flag in `simulate --help`.

Related pipeline stack: [visual native TSX reproduction #14](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/pull/14) → [accurate timeout diagnostic #15](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/pull/15). Inspect U1/U3 and the DQ/DQS/DQSn traces in that PCB rendering. The identical reduced 6,210-filament deck fails at a deliberate 100 ms deadline and completes in about 4.35 s with a 30-second deadline. This confirms deadline handling, not original-board convergence. This flag works with the current adapter API; the improved diagnostic separately needs a pipeline release and CLI dependency refresh because the CLI bundles it.

Additional local integration check (28 October): built this CLI branch with the merged pipeline at `a9c716a2bd60813f717a6994dc451f0deb8b6272`, then temporarily installed the resulting local CLI in the AM3352 board without saving dependency changes. The board's actual `tsci simulate` entry accepted the flag, and a deliberately bounded 100 ms run reached FastHenry and reported `native_timeout`. The native DDR composition test passed (63 assertions). No full extraction or eye was run. This is local validation; this PR still needs a newly packaged pipeline release and dependency refresh to bundle the diagnostic in a published CLI.

title: test: reproduce inaccessible native solver timeout setting
description: Reproduces a bug where the native solver timeout setting is inaccessible, ensuring that invalid timeout values are rejected and valid ones are forwarded correctly.
body:
`tsci simulate` always constructs `createNativeSolver()` without options, so a native PCB extraction cannot request more than the adapter's 900,000 ms per-process deadline. This regression renders a native TSX transient declaration through the command, then records options at the native process boundary in an isolated child. It checks that an explicit deadline reaches the adapter, omission retains the adapter default, and malformed values are rejected before rendering.

Run `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun test tests/cli/simulate/pcb-spice-timeout.test.ts`. On this reproduction branch, the default reaches the boundary but `--solver-timeout-ms 1800000` is an unknown option; the two assertions fail as intended and are marked `test.failing`, so CI remains green. The fix PR turns them into ordinary passing tests. No heavy solver executes and no waveform/eye is generated.

The real FastHenry reproduction, native U1/U3 DQ/DQS PCB visual, and diagnostic fix are in [pcb-spice-pipeline #14](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/pull/14) / [#15](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/pull/15). Review U1 on the left, U3 on the right, the three DQ/DQS/DQSn traces, and the lower ground pads/vias. That TSX reproduction preserves the original numerical extraction settings while reducing geometry. Its 6,210-filament refined extraction times out at 100 ms but completes in about 4.35 seconds with a 30-second deadline on the investigation machine.

Origin: AM3352 board `99b75cf9844894b4ad65ee9cb4669b6bcf575d88`, CLI 0.1.2418, native adapter default deadline. The original 284,695-filament run has not been retried; its timeout is inferred from elapsed duration, not a proven FastHenry numerical error. Raising a process deadline does not relax geometry, mesh or numerical acceptance. The fix is stacked in #5621.

title: fix: stop repeated preview refreshes during rapid edits
description: Fixes repeated browser preview refreshes caused by rapid filesystem saves triggering multiple uploads, by coalescing saves with a debounce mechanism.
body:
0hmx@dots

Rapid filesystem saves currently trigger an immediate file-server upload for every watcher event. This can rebuild the browser preview repeatedly, echo browser-originated writes back to the server, and leave concurrent uploads in flight.

Coalesce saves with a 250 ms trailing debounce and a 1 s maximum wait. Sync one batch at a time, reading current file contents when processing it and retaining edits received during an upload. Keep Chokidar's 100 ms atomic-save normalization explicit, suppress unchanged-content uploads (including browser writeback), and drain active work before shutting down the HTTP server. New local dependencies are uploaded before their importing source.

The delay is an interaction tradeoff, not a universal standard: [Chokidar documents atomic saves](https://github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/tree/4.0.1#performance), [webpack documents aggregating saves before rebuilding](https://webpack.js.org/configuration/watch/#watchoptionsaggregatetimeout), and [Lodash documents trailing debounce with maxWait](https://lodash.com/docs/#debounce). A bounded batch avoids the indefinite postponement that an unbounded quiet-period wait can cause during continuous edits.

Validation on macOS with Bun 1.3.14:
- New native TSX watcher tests cover single saves, a five-save burst, continuous editing, atomic rename saves, identical-content saves, ignored generated cache output, deletion, and disposal. Queue tests cover in-flight edits, errors/recovery, and cancellation. Additional regressions verify exact binary-byte comparison and browser text/binary writeback without duplicate uploads.
- The burst regression fails on the original code: five saves produced five uploads; the patch produces one and retains the final source.
- After review fixes, all 8 coalescing tests pass and the complete dev-server test group passes 31/31.
- Repository formatting, TypeScript check, and CLI build pass.
- ChatGPT in-app browser: five rapid fixture saves changed four uploads/two completed runs to one upload/one completed run when combined with the companion runframe fix. The selected view survived, syntax errors remained visible, and an atomic save recovered to the latest value. No document reload occurred during saves.

The companion [runframe PR #5927](https://github.com/tscircuit/runframe/pull/5927) handles active/pending render scheduling and keeps the previous completed preview visible. This CLI change also works with existing runframe versions. The full CLI command suite was not run locally; all five hosted Linux test shards, Windows tests, smoke init, formatting, types, dependency policy, and dependency ownership checks passed on `3c8cc4672f36ec12787655433edd3db0f76f5114`. No board-design changes are included.

Each PR can be reviewed independently. The combined behavior reaches standard CLI installations after the runframe fix is released and incorporated into the standalone browser bundle distributed with tscircuit; both changes are already active together in the tested local installation.

Review feedback addressed in `3c8cc46`: store cached contents consistently as byte buffers, removing the new `typeof`/`Buffer.isBuffer` guard, and split every added coalescing test into a separate file with shared fixture setup.

title: Show explosion guides and improve assembly preview framing
description: Adds support for rendering explosion guides in assembly previews and adjusts camera settings to fit full exported geometry, including off-board parts, while preserving authored explosion programs through GLTF conversion.
body:
Assembly previews currently omit motion guides and use a shallow, loosely fitted camera. Preserve the authored explosion program through native GLTF conversion, export guide paths as `scene.extras.poppygl.explosionLines`, and let PoppyGL render dashed overlays in PNG/SVG images. No guide meshes are added. Generic rotatable GLB viewers display the sampled geometry and may ignore the overlay metadata.

Fit the full exported geometry and guide endpoints with an elevated `assembly` camera preset, including tall and off-board parts. Existing PCB-only camera behavior stays unchanged. Version only the 3D cache so older images and GLBs without metadata are not reused after deployment.

Uses the published releases `circuit-json-to-gltf@0.0.160` and `poppygl@0.0.38`; [poppygl #55](https://github.com/tscircuit/poppygl/pull/55) and [circuit-json-to-gltf #276](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/276) are merged. Dependency overrides keep the image renderer and `tscircuit` on the same PoppyGL release. [Core #5009](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5009) updates the conventional source of these versions for the next `tscircuit` dependency sync. Companion docs layout changes are in [docs #976](https://github.com/tscircuit/docs/pull/976).

Validation on the released dependencies: 7 focused tests pass (363 assertions), covering TSX stage snapshots, metadata instead of guide meshes, PNG/SVG/GLB parity, compressed POST input, tall/offset assembly cameras, guide endpoints outside mesh bounds, dependency resolution, and 3D cache invalidation. TypeScript and production build pass. The earlier full Worker/cache and production smoke checks passed; those paths are unchanged by this dependency update.

title: Render assembly explosion stages in 3D images and GLB models
description: Add support for rendering assembly explosion stages in 3D images and GLB models, allowing users to visualize Circuit JSON explosion programs through CircuitPreview.
body:
The image service currently renders only the assembled pose, so docs cannot illustrate Circuit JSON explosion programs through CircuitPreview. Add `explosion_stage` and `explosion_progress` query/POST options for PNG, SVG, and GLB. Whole-stage targets move their members together; partial progress samples sequential moves from the original positions. Omission preserves the assembled view, and invalid requests return uncached HTTP 400 responses.

Sample with published core 0.0.2235 before the existing renderers, upgrade the GLTF exporter to 0.0.159 and Circuit JSON to 0.0.540, and keep TSX evaluation on the same core. Compressed Circuit JSON POST bodies and image CORS headers let the full RP2040 assembly fit within svg3's 1 MiB limit. The Next/Vercel adapter preserves text/plain JSON without double-encoding it. Image/model cache keys distinguish stage and progress while sharing geometry for the same pose.

Includes four PNG snapshots (assembled, cover and bolts lifted together, bolts halfway removed, bolts removed), TSX-to-JSON evaluation tests, PNG/SVG/GLB pose agreement, compressed POST validation, and cache isolation. The required core/footprinter upgrade changes the Biscuit Board LED fabrication symbol; its reviewed snapshot is refreshed, with board geometry and copper unchanged.

Validation:
- 36 focused API/cache tests pass on CI's Bun 1.3.14; root and worker TypeScript, production build, and formatting pass.
- Production smoke tests pass under both Bun and Node, including TSX export followed by partial-stage PNG/GLB requests using compressed text/plain POST bodies.
- All six poses of the full TSX-generated RP2040/NEMA17 assembly returned PNGs through the real HTTP server. Browser verification covered selecting poses, loading the matching GLB, and returning to an earlier stage.
- The deployed Vercel PR preview also returned HTTP 200 image/png with CORS for the full RP2040 board at halfway bolt removal, using the compressed POST request.
- Full local suite: 113 pass, 1 skip, 1 existing macOS PNG snapshot failure (`3d-infinite-grid-with-model`, 30.349% difference). Unchanged main reproduces the same failure and difference. The focused snapshot passes in isolation; its baseline is not changed here.

Enables [tscircuit/docs#976](https://github.com/tscircuit/docs/pull/976). Deploy this service change before merging the docs' live stage previews.

title: Add schematic_manifest and schematic_sheet for paging schematic sheets
description: Adds functionality to allow clients to display one schematic sheet at a time instead of a stacked SVG, including a manifest for pagination and rendering specific sheets.
body:
Lets clients show one schematic sheet at a time instead of the stacked SVG, mirroring `drawing_manifest` / `drawing_page`.

- `svg_type=schematic&schematic_manifest=true` returns `{ pages: [{ name, schematicSheetId, pageNumber }] }` in sheet order, with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` so browsers can read it (the stacked schematic SVG has no CORS header). Circuits without sheets return `pages: []`.
- `schematic_sheet=N` renders only that sheet via `convertCircuitJsonToSchematicSvg({ schematicSheetId })`, with `X-Schematic-Sheet` / `X-Schematic-Sheet-Count` headers. Invalid values return an uncached 400.
- Without either parameter, output is unchanged.

The svg3 cache bypasses JSON responses, so the manifest keeps its CORS header.

Used by the docs `CircuitPreview` schematic pager (PR to follow in tscircuit/docs).

Tested: new `tests/schematic-sheet-pages.test.ts`, existing schematic tests, and `tsc`.

title: Update eval to 0.0.1661, core to 0.0.2222 and props to 0.0.714
description: Updates the evaluator and core dependencies to their latest versions, enabling the rendering of test-point pads in autorouting phase.
body:
Updates the evaluator to a current core. svg.tscircuit.com renders code with `CircuitRunner` from `@tscircuit/eval/eval`, which bundles its own core. The exact pin `@tscircuit/eval@0.0.1552` (from #2399) meant rendering ran on core ~0.0.2095, even though `@tscircuit/core` here was 0.0.2205. The automated update workflow only bumps `tscircuit`, so eval had not moved since September.

- `@tscircuit/eval` 0.0.1552 → **0.0.1661** (bundles core 0.0.2222 and props 0.0.714)
- `@tscircuit/core` 0.0.2205 → **0.0.2222**
- `@tscircuit/props` 0.0.710 → **0.0.714**

This makes `<autoroutingphase reroute addTestPoints />` (tscircuit/core#4974) render, so the preview in tscircuit/docs#970 shows its generated test-point pads. Props 0.0.714 is required: older props schemas silently strip `addTestPoints`.

The existing compatibility holds from #2399 (`biscuitboard`, `@tscircuit/fanout-solver`, `circuit-json-to-gltf`) are unchanged.

**Tests**
- New `tests/autoroutingphase-test-points.test.ts` renders the docs example through the server (`format=circuit_json`) and expects two `TP_AUTO_*` test points.
- `bun test tests`: 109 pass, 1 skipped. No snapshots changed.
- `standard usb_c connector resolves in pcb svg` is skipped. The parts engine now picks a different part for `standard="usb_c"` (JLCPCB C2765186, `TYPE-C 16PIN 2MD(073)`, an SMD receptacle instead of the through-hole part in the snapshot). Main's own dependencies render the same new part, so this test fails on main too. The test now sets that MPN, but core ignores `manufacturerPartNumber` for standard connectors, so it can't pin the part yet. Re-enable it and update the snapshot after the core fix.
- `bun run format:check` passes.

title: docs(symbol): sizing a symbol (width / height, fit, viewbox)
description: Adds a Sizing a Symbol section to the symbol  page, detailing how width, height, fit, and viewbox properties affect symbol rendering in schematics.
body:
Adds a "Sizing a Symbol" section to the `<symbol />` page, covering the props that landed for tscircuit/core#4698 (props#943 in 0.0.704, core#4706 / #4705):

- how `width` / `height` fit the drawing: `fit="fill"` (the default) and `"stretch"` scale each axis separately, and `fit="contain"` keeps the proportions;
- `viewbox={{ minX, maxX, minY, maxY }}`, the region of the symbol's own coordinates that gets fitted, and why the default bounds include the port stubs.

The preview compares a stretched contact with a round one. I checked it against @tscircuit/core 0.0.2171: the contained contact draws at exactly 1 mm with its port 1 mm out. The current `tscircuit` release (0.0.2935) still bundles core 0.0.2170, so the preview shows the new behaviour once the docs site picks up 0.0.2171.

title: Expose bounded power passes with route and width comparisons
description: Updates the power-trace-expander to expose powerTraceExpansion with a maximum of one expansion pass, allowing for shorter expansion at the cost of latency on small boards, while providing beforeafter comparisons and DRC records for a motherboard.
body:
Update power-trace-expander to expose `powerTraceExpansion: { maxExpansionPasses: 1 }`, and add reproducible motherboard before/after PNGs and per-category DRC records inside bugreport110. The default remains four passes: shorter expansion is opt-in because it trades additional widening for latency on small boards.

With one pass enabled, the dedicated power-board benchmark completes all six scenarios with zero relaxed DRC errors, unchanged via count, median 1.94 s → 1.43 s (-26.4%), and P95 7.41 s → 3.25 s (-56.2%). [Benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41154389810). Remaining normalized width deficit rises by 0.34–3.37 percentage points on these boards; DRC alone does not capture that tradeoff. The benchmark used the earlier commit that enabled one pass by default; the final API requires the explicit option for equivalent behavior.

On the motherboard, one pass retains widening that the original search discards after exhausting its budget. Relaxed DRC errors fall 1,307 → 1,303 with no category increasing. Reproduce with `POWER_EXPANSION_PASSES=4` or `1` when running `fixtures/bug-reports/bugreport110-motherboard-power-phase/profile-full-route.ts`. Local timings are omitted from the committed comparison. The isolated full-board ABBA comparison combining #3397, #3405 and this enabled policy improves 210.997 s → 195.740 s (7.23%), below the 10% full-board target. Both candidate outputs are identical, with 761 traces. [Timing, route and quality artifacts](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41154348644).

Depends on tscircuit/power-trace-expander#66 and is stacked on #3397. The dependency's 99 tests, types, build and CI pass; focused Pipeline9 power integration tests pass. `/benchmark --dataset 18` completes all 16 scenarios with zero relaxed DRC errors and no outcome regressions; median +0.5%, P95 +1.4%. [Dataset 18 results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41154360800).

title: Avoid repeating identical A01 connection-order searches
description: Eliminates redundant A01 connection-order searches by deduplicating initial orderings, improving efficiency in adaptive portfolio expansion.
body:
Adaptive portfolio expansion tries six shuffle seeds, but distinct seeds can yield the same initial connection ordering. A01 uses its seed only for that initial shuffle, so these candidates repeat the same deterministic search. Record each initial ordering after setup and omit duplicate adaptive candidates, retaining the first candidate even after its working queue changes.

The motherboard reproduction removes approximately 4.6 million repeated A01 steps and preserves final route JSON and SVG output. A full isolated ABBA run against main, including #3397's connectivity update, measures 208.775 s → 200.979 s (-3.73%); all four runs have the same route hash, 761 traces and 1,307 pre-existing relaxed DRC errors. This does **not** establish an additional end-to-end speedup over the connectivity change alone. [ABBA artifacts](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41153685593).

`/benchmark --dataset 18`: 16/16 completion and DRC pass, zero errors/outcome regressions; median -2.7%, P95 -4.0%, P60/P80 +3.6%/+3.5%. [Dataset comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41153520852).

Rebased onto current main after #3397 and #3403 were squash-merged. The solver changes contain only the ordering deduplication and its regression test; they use main's published connectivity dependency. The test workflow also pins Ubuntu 24.04: the ubuntu-latest migration to 26.04 caused the same 11 native routing snapshot failures on main and this PR. No snapshots or tolerances were changed. After rebasing: 21 portfolio tests pass (1,174 assertions) and TypeScript passes. The regression test retains initial-order identity after queue mutation. All nine test shards and the build, type, format, dependency and deployment checks pass on commit 40f8c0b. [Green CI run](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41171400636). Benchmark figures above refer to the original measured revisions.

body:
Replace `@tscircuit/checks` calls in autorouter execution with local DRC evaluators, covering Pipeline 9 joint repair, cleanup, precision-margin measurement, and A13 board validation. Preserve the reference clearance rules, connectivity, error ordering, metadata, and repair locations.

Performance changes are separated into the stacked follow-up #3375. This PR establishes the native evaluator implementation and removes runtime calls to `checks`.

Keep the evaluator's existing `inputSrj` name and input data unchanged. Reuse the existing Circuit JSON conversion and connectivity helper from `lib/utils`, the existing DRC options from `lib/types`, shared clearance defaults, and the math library's `Point` and `Bounds` types. The converter implementations are moved unchanged; their old testing import paths re-export the shared implementations.

The implementation uses public geometry and connectivity APIs. Continuity no longer calls `PcbConnectivityMap._arePcbTracesConnected` or populates that class's internal fields. The segment contact predicate retains its bounds guard and tolerance, including very short copper segments.

Validation on `30e5c940`:
- Four critical test files cover the no-checks subprocess guard, full-evaluator parity, continuity, and error ordering (84 local assertions).
- The subprocess guard disables every checks function, exercises routing, cleanup, exact joint repair, and A13 validation, then independently checks successful routing outputs.
- Exact continuity parity across 92 SRJ18/SRJ23 fixtures preserves all 497 reference errors, including when identifiers are replaced with opaque names.
- All nine CI test shards, build, type checking, formatting, code-policy checks, dependency-patch checks, and deployment passed on head `30e5c940`. Local focused tests, type checking, and build also passed.
- Audit found no dataset-specific branches, dependency patches, error suppression, reduced clearance rules, or changes to benchmark configuration.

Historical performance baseline: [same-machine SRJ18 comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3354#issuecomment-6522201945) for removal-only `6989647` against the pre-removal base `e703f04` completed and passed DRC on 16/16 samples with unchanged via counts, but median routing time was 8.7% slower and P90 was 8.8% slower. This PR does not claim a speed improvement; #3375 addresses the native evaluator overhead.

The only added dependency, `@flatten-js/core`, supplies non-circular-hole geometry and nearest-point repair locations. It is already transitive through `@tscircuit/circuit-json-util` and is declared explicitly for direct imports. `@tscircuit/checks` remains for independent tests and as a transitive dependency.

title: Optimize native autorouter continuity evaluation
description: Optimizes continuity evaluation in the autorouter by caching connectivity through shared pads and reducing unnecessary geometry construction during routing candidate evaluation.
body:
Native continuity scoring introduced by #3354 repeatedly formats diagnostic names and constructs copper geometry while evaluating routing candidates. Cache connectivity through shared pads, format names only when reporting an error, and construct copper polygons only for segments near layer bridges. Preserve exact contact tests, tolerances, and error results.

**Stacked on #3354**, targeting `codex/remove-checks-from-autorouter`. This PR contains two performance commits affecting only the continuity implementation and its existing test.

The pad-connectivity cache proves positive connections; candidates without that proof still go through the complete geometric connectivity evaluation. Spatial bounds conservatively select possible contacts, then the original precise polygon contact test decides connectivity. Caches are scoped to each candidate evaluation. There are no dataset-specific paths or changes to benchmark settings.

### Same-machine SRJ18 benchmark

[Fresh results for the current stack](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3375#issuecomment-6524883749): removal-only parent `30e5c940` and optimization head `568c2499` ran sequentially on one 8-vCPU Blacksmith ARM runner. Both used all 16 SRJ18 samples, four workers, effort 1, and a 600-second sample timeout.

| Metric | Removal only | Optimized | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| P50 routing time | 34.1 s | 32.6 s | -4.3% |
| P80 routing time | 79.8 s | 71.4 s | -10.4% |
| P90 routing time | 111.0 s | 108.6 s | -2.2% |
| Joint DRC repair, summed stage time | 151.553 s | 106.275 s | -29.9% |
| Memory P50 | 1342.0 MiB | 1309.6 MiB | -2.4% |
| Memory P80 | 2274.3 MiB | 2333.2 MiB | +2.6% |
| Memory P90 | 2786.1 MiB | 2655.3 MiB | -4.7% |

Both revisions completed and passed reference DRC on 16/16 samples, with zero DRC issues and zero timeouts. Raw reports confirm unchanged via counts, trace counts, and lint results for every sample, using identical runtime settings. Performance changes are relative to #3354, which already removes runtime `checks` calls.

### Validation

- Four critical regression tests passed with 88 assertions, including the subprocess guard that disables every checks function and independently validates routing outputs.
- Exact SRJ18/SRJ23 continuity parity preserved all 497 reference errors across 92 fixtures, also with opaque identifiers, against both the previous implementation and independent checks.
- All nine CI test shards passed on the rebased head `568c2499`; local focused tests, build, and type checking also passed. The repository's build, type-check, and format workflows target PRs to `main` and run on the parent PR.
- No new dependencies or additional test files are introduced by this optimization PR.

body:
Reduce repeated collision geometry work and A* allocation overhead without changing routing decisions or iteration budgets.

The desktop motherboard full-route comparison is **91.30 s → 80.22 s (12.1% faster)** in four fresh Bun 1.4.2 processes, run in ABBA order on the same desktop. Baseline source was restored from the original pinned revisions in the same installed dependency tree. Routing time excludes DRC, rendering, hashing and serialization.

| Run | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First | 93.28 s | 79.76 s |
| Second | 89.33 s | 80.68 s |
| Mean | 91.30 s | 80.22 s |

High-density routing falls from 50.33 s to 46.65 s (7.3%); power expansion from 19.80 s to 13.44 s (32.1%). All four runs produce byte-identical route JSON and SVG: 761 traces, 10,633,725 outer iterations, and the same 1,307 pre-existing relaxed DRC findings. This performance change does not make the motherboard DRC-clean.

Changes:
- Store native heap priorities separately and reject visited neighbors before allocating full candidate state, preserving tie order.
- Integrate [A01 #136](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-a01/pull/136): avoid unnecessary occupancy lookups and path-state allocation for dominated arrivals while retaining queue entries and search-budget accounting.
- Integrate [power expander #65](https://github.com/tscircuit/power-trace-expander/pull/65): exact segment capsules, prepared per-blocker clearance bounds, early-exit boolean geometry, and deferred copying until a local inflation succeeds.
- The collision query uses the public API proposed in [Flatbush #75](https://github.com/mourner/flatbush/pull/75), pinned to a packaged fork revision with generated declarations and a distinct prerelease version. Dependency PRs should merge before this integration.

Validation:
- All autorouter CI checks pass; this PR and both tscircuit dependency PRs are mergeable.
- 8 focused native tests / 84,794 assertions, 4 A01 tests / 363,278 assertions, 98 power-expander tests / 139,831 assertions, and 20 Flatbush tests.
- [Final `/benchmark --dataset 18`](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41018210083): 16/16 complete, 16/16 relaxed DRC passes, no timeouts, identical non-timing snapshots. P50 30.2 → 30.4 s (+0.4%), P90 101.1 → 100.4 s (-0.7%), P95 106.5 → 103.9 s (-2.4%). Memory P50 +0.2%, P90 +1.3%. The dataset-wide median is essentially flat; this is not a claim of 10% improvement on every board. Dataset 18 does not exercise power expansion.
- [Clean-checkout Blacksmith motherboard ABBA comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/41018777894): **223.67 → 205.88 s (8.0% faster)**. Baseline runs: 216.46 / 230.88 s; candidate runs: 203.22 / 208.53 s. Power expansion 48.45 → 33.94 s (30.0%); high-density routing 119.67 → 116.84 s (2.4%). All four Linux runs have byte-identical route JSON and SVG, 761 traces, 10,633,724 outer iterations, and 1,307 existing relaxed DRC findings. Cross-platform output hashes differ; equality is asserted within each comparison. The 10% target is met on desktop, but not on the dedicated Linux runner.

The captured workload and reproduction runner remain in numbered bugreport110. Supersedes exploratory draft #3370.

title: Reduce power-expansion collision searches on irrelevant layers
description: Reduces the number of spatial candidates in power expansion by indexing collision searches by layer, resulting in a significant decrease in irrelevant candidates and improved processing time.
body:
Power expansion on motherboard bugreport110 retrieved 130 million spatial candidates, 63% on irrelevant copper layers. Pin [power-trace-expander #63](https://github.com/tscircuit/power-trace-expander/pull/63), which lazily indexes boolean collision searches by layer while preserving exact shapes, through-via coverage and ordered collision-list behavior.

Four fresh-process, unprofiled expansion runs in ABBA order measured **24.206/21.942/21.921/24.321 seconds**: a 9.6% stage improvement, about 2.3 seconds, with identical output and 7,751,939 iterations. This is not a 9.6% whole-pipeline improvement. Memory varied across runs; no memory reduction is claimed.

The numbered bugreport110 directory contains the probes, raw results and analysis. It also records two remaining opportunities (85,829 repeated endpoint queries and allocation before endpoint rejection) and rejects an inert-force hypothesis: none of 458 million endpoint interactions in this fixture was inert.

Validation: all 92 existing dependency tests pass without snapshot changes; a new layer-index differential test adds 5,605 assertions. Dependency build/typecheck pass. The complete motherboard comparison passes locally with exact output hash `5c90f0d5e4bd73b4aed32d62e1f4350e5df0f36a70c53d47a2a79d714d7ab974`; typecheck passes. All applicable CI checks are green at `f859515`, including the full motherboard comparison. Dataset 18 completed as a pipeline control; it scarcely exercises power expansion, so the captured-stage replay provides direct coverage.

No changes to routing effort, iteration budgets, acceptance rules or existing DRC findings. No top-level scripts or snapshot updates.


The post-change probe returns 52,956,323 candidates rather than 129,982,687 (-59.3%). The remaining 5,070,774 foreign-layer candidates are in unchanged global-query APIs. Endpoint counts and output remain identical.

The benchmark uses `1bb7296`. The only subsequent commit, `f859515`, wraps a diagnostic declaration for CI style and records the post-change counters; routing source and dependency pins are unchanged.

Further investigation: a diagnostic DRC pass observed 499,142 cached queries, 176,566 hits, 322,576 misses and 287,884 evictions. Geometry changes legitimately invalidate some reuse. The profile attributes about 6.2 sampled seconds to cached DRC queries versus only 0.28 to repeated expansion endpoint checks, so DRC cache bookkeeping merits investigation first. This PR does not change DRC caching.


### Completed dataset 18 control

[Results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3356#issuecomment-6503753081): 16/16 complete and relaxed-DRC-clean on both revisions, zero timeouts, unchanged via and angled-trace counts. Median runtime increased 36.1s -> 38.0s (+5.1%) and P90 increased 116.3s -> 119.4s (+2.6%) in this single paired run. P90 memory decreased 2.4%. This is not evidence of a broad speedup or a blanket no-performance-regression claim; the isolated expansion ABBA runs establish the targeted gain.

The stage report shows only 0.001s of power-expansion steps across the dataset, but this counter excludes constructor setup. Inspection found that `PowerTraceExpansionSolver` constructs the full expander before checking `onlyConnectionNames.length === 0`; this is another candidate for wasted-work investigation, not fixed in this PR. Do not interpret the step counter as total constructor-inclusive cost.

title: Speed up complete motherboard power-phase routing without changing output
description: Optimizes the motherboard power-phase routing process by indexing nearby boundary candidates, significantly reducing processing time while maintaining output integrity.
body:
The motherboard power-phase fixture wastes time projecting preloaded copper onto every graph boundary and repeatedly rebuilding 110,538 cells for two rectangular copper planes. Index nearby boundary candidates before exact checks, and pin the compatible power-expander fix from https://github.com/tscircuit/power-trace-expander/pull/62. The expander indexes every rectangular obstacle as one exact polygon (without pour-specific branches or an Infinity cell-size sentinel) and avoids rebuilding unchanged parent statistics during child searches. Clearance rules, effort and iteration budgets are preserved.

**Recorded complete routing before the general-rectangle follow-up, with CPU profiling disabled:** same captured input, fresh processes, Bun 1.4.2/macOS M3 Pro, effort 1, no cache/workers.

| Measurement | Original | Preload fix only | Both fixes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Complete routing | 174.84 s | 135.06 s | 107.33 s |
| Power expansion | 56.09 s | 55.95 s | 28.33 s |
| Output traces | 761 | 761 | 761 |

This saves **38.6% overall (1.63x faster)** and 20.5% versus the preload-only fix. These are individual runs, not statistical medians. The earlier 423.81/109.36-second comparison included CPU profiling, which disproportionately slowed the original implementation; its 3.88x ratio is not a normal-runtime speedup.

The reference DRC evaluator omitted via-to-pad copper clearance, so it could report zero errors for a board rejected by the board checker. This PR checks the declared via/pad copper rules, attributes violations to the owning routes, and repairs them without weakening clearance or connectivity validation.

Stacked on #3147. The stack is rebased onto current main and its merge conflicts are resolved.

- Apply the stricter via-specific/general pad clearance consistently in reference DRC, Pipeline7/9 scoring, Pipeline11 validation, simplification, and power expansion. Preserve explicit zero and existing defaults; keep copper and drill rules separate.
- Preserve physical and reference validation before publishing partial repairs. Via-pad residue must retain its obstacle/route ownership and cannot worsen. Cache only exact-geometry reference results.
- Repair shared physical vias together while keeping preloaded copper and geometry outside the local repair region fixed. This clears the MIDI keyboard USB regression.
- Keep initial clearance projection local to reported errors. Global smoothing previously moved distant clean routes into pads and caused a valid repair to be rejected. SRJ33 sample 13 now has zero relaxed DRC errors and the baseline's 117 vias.
- Keep the configured coarse grid for the first regional search, then refine it when the existing region expands. This preserves the Linux OV9281 repair and clears SRJ33 sample 26's remaining narrow crossing within the original search allowance. The captured Linux regression clears all 186 initial errors without entering broad repair or adding vias.

title: repro: via drilled into a BGA pad fails topology merging
description: Reproduces a bug where a via drilled into a BGA pad causes topology merging to fail in Pipeline 9.
body:
A via drilled into a BGA pad (via-in-pad) makes Pipeline 9 throw in `TopologyMergingSolver`:

```
TopologyMergingSolver: output nodes "obstacle-pcb_component_0-…:top-0--0.4--0.4" and "cmn_13" have an unresolved inter-group overlap on a shared layer
```

This PR adds the reproduction only. Production code is unchanged. The fix is stacked on top in #3333.

### Reproduction

`fixtures/bug-reports/via-in-pad-topology-overlap/` holds a 4-layer board with a 6x6, 0.8mm-pitch BGA. A 0.3mm through via sits at the center of the 0.4mm pad of the inner ball at (-0.4, -0.4), on the same net, and that ball connects to a resistor about 7mm away. tscircuit/core 0.0.2222 emitted this SRJ from a `<via>` placed in the pad (the case reported on a user's AM3352 board). It includes a debugger fixture.

Two tests pin the current behavior:
- `tests/bugs/via-in-pad-topology-overlap.test.ts`: the full Pipeline 9 run throws the overlap error.
- `tests/bugs/via-in-pad-topology-overlap-unit.test.ts`: a minimal `TopologyMergingSolver` case (a global via target inside a larger component pad target on z0) throws the same error.

### Cause

Inside the pad, `getLayerTopologiesForCoveredNodes` correctly lets the global via target own z0, so the component pad target is dropped there. `restoreAuthoritativeTargetRegions` then restores the pad to its full source bounds anyway, because its source key only ever appeared in `target-passthrough` regions. The restored pad overlaps the via on z0.

title: fix(TopologyMergingSolver): via-in-pad no longer throws an inter-group overlap
description: Fixes autorouting failure when a via-in-pad causes an inter-group overlap error in the TopologyMergingSolver.
body:
Stacked on #3334, which adds the reproduction. Merge that first.

## Problem

A via drilled into a BGA pad (via-in-pad) makes Pipeline 9 throw:

```
TopologyMergingSolver: output nodes "obstacle-pcb_component_0-…:top-0--0.4--0.4" and "cmn_13" have an unresolved inter-group overlap on a shared layer
```

On the pad's layer, three target-obstacle nodes cover the via area: the component group's pad node, the component group's via node, and the global mesh's via node (`cmn_13`). `getLayerTopologiesForCoveredNodes` correctly lets the global target own that area (`target-passthrough` with global authoritative nodes), so the pad is dropped there.

`restoreAuthoritativeTargetRegions` then restores the pad to its full source bounds, because its source key only ever appeared in `target-passthrough` regions. It didn't account for the pad having been overruled elsewhere. The restored pad overlaps `cmn_13` on z0, and `validateTopologyMergingOutput` throws.

## Fix

`getLayerTopologiesForCoveredNodes` also returns the component target source keys that lose a layer to a global target. The solver collects them, and `restoreAuthoritativeTargetRegions` doesn't restore those. They keep their exact atomic regions around the global target.

Nets aren't involved. The bug was the restore step ignoring which node owned that layer.

## Tests

The two repro tests from #3334 now assert the fixed behavior:
- `tests/bugs/via-in-pad-topology-overlap.test.ts`: Pipeline 9 solves the BGA fixture and routes the trace.
- `tests/bugs/via-in-pad-topology-overlap-unit.test.ts`: the global via target keeps its full node, and the component pad keeps everything except the via's area.

Locally: `tsc --noEmit` is clean and all topology tests pass. I also ran a sweep of 313 Pipeline 7/9, BGA and via test files (non-benchmark) on the fix: 339 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped.

Related: tscircuit/core#4983 avoids emitting the overlapping pad/via obstacles in core. This PR makes the solver handle the case regardless of what produced the input.

Four fresh-process passes on one 8-vCPU ARM64 Blacksmith runner, Bun 1.4.2. Serial passes run three concurrent samples; four-thread passes run one sample at a time.

| Metric | Original 1T | Prepared 1T | Original 4T | Prepared 4T |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Completion / relaxed DRC pass | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 | 16/16 |
| DRC issues / timeouts | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| Summed port-point stage time | 137.276 s | 85.589 s | 153.272 s | 88.259 s |
| Summed full-pipeline time | 767.404 s | 725.794 s | 622.705 s | 520.250 s |
| Full-pipeline P50 | 34.320 s | 32.538 s | 25.079 s | 22.015 s |
| Full-pipeline P90 | 115.193 s | 113.105 s | 84.147 s | 72.025 s |
| Memory P90 | 2438.4 MiB | 2571.0 MiB | 2409.4 MiB | 2709.4 MiB |

Four-thread port-point time falls **42.4%** across all 16 samples. Summed full-pipeline time falls **16.5%**, P50 falls **12.2%**, and P90 falls **14.4%**. All recorded logical port-point routing metrics match across all four passes.

Sample006:

| Metric | Original 1T | Prepared 1T | Original 4T | Prepared 4T |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Port-point stage | 37.905 s | 20.417 s | 39.879 s | 20.665 s |
| Full pipeline | 86.222 s | 68.390 s | 72.621 s | 52.820 s |

Sample006's four-thread stage is **1.930× faster than original 4T**; its full pipeline is **27.3% faster**. There is **no serial slowdown**: serial port-point time falls 37.7% across the dataset and 46.1% on sample006.

The measured trade-off is memory: four-thread P90 peak RSS rises **12.5%**, about 300 MiB. Full-pipeline sample016 is 0.23 s slower in this single pass; the other 15 samples are faster. There are no completion or DRC regressions.

[Workflow and raw artifact](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/40458289229).

### SolverRuntime and determinism

`RegionDistancePreparationSolver` runs at most four static geometry chunks through the caller-owned SolverRuntime pool, with standard Bun and Node registrations. Serial execution runs the same jobs inline. Results are assembled in fixed chunk order; worker timing never influences routing.

**Route searches and commits remain serial.** Most improvement comes from cheaper search operations. This is an exact-output optimization with parallel preparation; it does not demonstrate four-way search scaling. No custom worker protocol or dependency patches.

Marginal cost tables use an integer crossing/via index and are invalidated when native intersection caches change. Partial searches use native handling. Distance tables are capped at 128 MiB; general incidence and non-dense storage retain native expansion. Worker failures propagate without starting route search.

### Pre-extraction repeated local timing and validation

Three fresh-process repetitions per mode, rotated order, effort 1, cache disabled, Bun 1.4.4, four-CPU quota. Sample006 stage medians, including setup/preparation/worker lifecycle/search/section completion: original **21.720 s**, prepared serial **14.099 s**, prepared four workers **14.110 s**. Four workers are 1.539× faster than the original; prepared serial is 35.1% faster. Revised serial/four-worker medians are essentially equal.

- All nine repeated local outputs match the original byte for byte.
- All 16 local dataset18 port-point outputs match the original byte for byte.
- All 16 samples complete locally with four workers and zero relaxed DRC errors.
- Build, full TypeScript check, and **all nine CI test shards pass**.
- 11 focused tests cover original/serial/one/four-worker equality, nonzero density cost, forced final acceptance, reversed completion order, pool reuse, worker errors, general incidence, and async iteration budgets.
- Built Node v24.19.0 package passes four-worker full-pipeline parity and cleanup.

Abstract single-layer crossings already appear in the original stage output on samples 14 and 15. The harness records those diagnostics and verifies exact output equality; final board correctness is evaluated by full-pipeline relaxed DRC.

The seven autorouter formatting issues are fixed in `0fe023b`, following the explicit request to format these files. A clean-checkout formatting check and all eight runtime integration tests pass locally. **All CI checks are green at `0fe023b`: formatting, all nine test shards, types, package build, Vercel build, dependency-patch check, and string-ID check.**

Reproduction, raw local timings, and per-sample hashes: `experiments/deterministic-portpoint/{DESIGN.txt,RESULTS.txt,runtime-results.json,dataset18-output-parity.json}`.

title: Render Circuit JSON explosion stages and named playback frames
description: Render the new cad_explosion_stage and cad_explosion_move records directly, allowing users to select a stage and fractional progress for assembly playback without mutating the input.
body:
Render the new `cad_explosion_stage` and `cad_explosion_move` records directly. Callers can select a stage and fractional progress with `convertCircuitJsonToGltf(json, { explosion: { throughStageRef, stageProgress } })`; omitting the option keeps the assembly assembled.

`getAssemblyExplosionFrames(json)` returns a named assembled frame followed by every completed stage in playback order. Each frame provides conversion options, evaluated Circuit JSON and guide points, so a snapshot renderer can keep one camera and label each stage. These are static poses for scrubbing/storyboards, not glTF animation tracks.

Whole-stage targets expand explicit membership, preserve prior displacement and deduplicate overlapping targets. Sequential moves, reference surfaces, forward stage references and repeated/backward playback work without mutating the input. Validate all instructions before partial playback and reject missing identities, invalid ordering, mismatched membership, nonfinite movement and PCB-containing targets. Translation is applied in circuit-world XYZ before the existing exporter coordinate conversion. Both browser entry points use the same playback path; the legacy browser entry now handles boardless mechanical CAD through the full converter.

Use published `circuit-json@^0.0.539` instead of the previous schema preview, and require `circuit-json>=0.0.539` for consumers of the new runtime schemas. No runtime dependency on core is introduced. Core's companion PR [#4990](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4990) adds four annotated visual regressions, including all four stages of the real RP2040/NEMA17 assembly and an intermediate bolt-removal pose. The cover and entire bolt stage lift together before the parts separate; the README embeds the annotated TSX snapshot.

Validation: all **445 tests pass in CI**, alongside browser tests, typecheck, formatting and the preview build. The new four-panel snapshot was visually inspected and uses a 0.2% pixel-difference threshold. A negative control that removes the whole-stage sideways translation fails the snapshot as expected. Native and both browser entry points agree on emitted glTF origins.

![Native stage playback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/feat/assembly-explosion-stages/tests/snapshot/__snapshots__/assembly-explosion-stages.snap.png)

title: Load occt-import-js at runtime so bundlers don't package it
description: Changes the loading mechanism of occt-import-js to prevent bundlers from packaging it, allowing for runtime imports instead.
body:
STEP loading imported `occt-import-js` and `occt-import-js/dist/occt-import-js.wasm?url` with string literals. The `as string` casts only affect TypeScript, so bundlers still followed them. Core imports this package for assembly drawing dimensions, so eval's webworker inlined the 7.6 MB occt WASM as a **10.1 MB** data URL, plus occt's Node-only `require("path")`.

**Changes** (`lib/loaders/step.ts`)
- occt-import-js is imported through a function parameter (`importAtRuntime(specifier)`), so no bundler can follow it, even after minifiers inline constants. A first attempt using a `const` specifier was inlined back into `import(...)` by eval's esbuild minifier.
- Under Node/Bun it imports `occt-import-js` from `node_modules`, as before. In browsers it loads `occt-import-js@0.0.23` (`/+esm`) and its WASM from jsDelivr.
- New export `setOcctImportJs(factory, { wasmUrl })` lets apps supply their own copy or a self-hosted WASM, e.g. when CDN access isn't allowed.
- A failed load clears the cached promise so it can be retried.

**Verification**
- `bun test tests/`: 408 pass, 0 fail, including tests that parse real `.step` fixtures through occt under Bun. `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- In Chromium, the jsDelivr ESM build plus the CDN WASM parse `tests/assets/Contact.step` (1 mesh, 1498 triangles).
- Eval webworker (tscircuit/eval#5427) built with this change: no occt code or WASM in the bundle, and it drops from 30.2 MB to 20.0 MB. Combined with #269, eval builds with its original config (no resvg plugin, no `fs`/`os`/`path` externals), and all 4 Playwright browser tests pass.

Note: browsers without access to jsDelivr need `setOcctImportJs` to load STEP models.

title: Make resvg browser-safe and use @tscircuit/image-utils for PNG snapshots
description: Allows browser bundlers to include circuit-json-to-gltf without special handling for resvgresvg-js by loading it lazily and updating the PNG snapshot matcher to use tscircuitimage-utils.
body:
Lets browser bundlers include circuit-json-to-gltf without special handling for `@resvg/resvg-js`. This came up in tscircuit/eval#5427: core now imports this package, and eval's webworker build needed an esbuild plugin to stub resvg.

**Problem:** `lib/utils/svg-to-png.ts` imports `@resvg/resvg-js` statically. `board-renderer` only loads that module lazily, but a bundler without code splitting (eval's worker uses `splitting: false`) inlines the chunk and moves the static import to the top of the bundle. The import then either fails to build (native binding, `fs`/`os`/`path`) or, if marked external, fails to load in browsers.

**Changes**
- `svg-to-png.ts` now loads `Resvg` with `await import("@resvg/resvg-js")` at render time (the options type is still a type-only import).
- `package.json` gets a `browser` field mapping `@resvg/resvg-js`, `fs`, `os` and `path` to `false`. In browser bundles the native path then throws, and `board-renderer` already catches that and falls back to its canvas renderer. Node and Bun ignore the field.
- The PNG snapshot matcher uses `@tscircuit/image-utils/looks-same` (no sharp) instead of `looks-same`. The diff fraction is now `differentPixels / totalPixels` instead of the cluster bounding-box area, and the diff image comes from `looksSame.createDiff`.

**Verification**
- `bun test tests/`: 408 pass, 0 fail (same as main). `tsc --noEmit` passes.
- Swapping one snapshot for a different PNG makes the matcher fail and write a `.diff.png`.
- Dropping this build into eval: the webworker builds with no resvg plugin and no `fs`/`os` externals, and all 4 Playwright browser tests pass. Eval still needs `external: ["path"]` because occt-import-js calls `require("path")` (Node-only), and its own `browser` field maps `fs` but not `path`.

`format:check` fails on main already (`tests/fixtures/scaffold-board-lrg-lrg.json`, `dist/`); the changed files are formatted.

title: fix: export pcb_cutout geometry, including rounded rect corners
description: Fixes the STEP export to correctly include pcb_cutout geometry, ensuring cutouts pierce the board solid and are accurately represented in mechanical CAD.
body:
Fixes the STEP half of https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/3302.

## Summary

- Cut `pcb_cutout` elements out of the exported board solid. They were previously ignored entirely, so every board exported solid where it should have been pierced.
- Support `circle`, `rect` (including `rotation`) and `polygon` cutouts, and honour `corner_radius` on rect cutouts as true cylindrical corner faces rather than sharp corners.
- Add `repro05` and `repro06`, which assert against the OCCT-imported mesh that cutouts genuinely pierce both board faces and leave material where they should.

## Why this matters

The point of a STEP export is to drop the board into mechanical CAD and check fit against an enclosure, standoffs, a shaft, a bearing tower. Cutouts are precisely the features a mechanical assembly keys off — they are where something passes through the board. A board that exports solid disagrees with the fabricated part at exactly the features being designed around, and it does so silently: the outline comes through fine, so the export looks plausible until you try to mate it against something.

This bites hardest on non-rectangular boards, which are also the boards most likely to be exported to CAD in the first place. Concrete case that prompted this: a 71.5 mm jog-wheel module with a 36-point outline and four polygon cutouts for a bearing-carrier tower. The outline exported correctly; the four cutouts vanished, so the board arrived in CAD as a solid disc with nowhere for the tower to pass through. Because it is fab-critical geometry, the failure mode is worse than a missing preview — a board fabricated from this data cannot be corrected afterwards.

This continues the non-rectangular board correctness work in #121, #123 and #125, which fixed outline and hole wall loops in the same solid.

## What changed

`circuitJsonToStep` only ever collected `pcb_hole` and `pcb_plated_hole`. `pcb_cutout` is now collected alongside them and turned into the same bottom-loop / top-loop / wall-faces structure that holes already produce, so cutouts flow through the existing inner-bound and shell assembly unchanged.

- `circle` reuses the existing circular hole geometry (`radius * 2` feeds the `hole_diameter` path), producing the same cylindrical wall as a drilled hole.
- `rect` and `polygon` go through a new segment-based boundary builder in `lib/cutout-geometry.ts`. A boundary is a list of straight lines and counter-clockwise arcs; straight segments get planar wall faces and arcs get cylindrical ones.
- Incoming polygon points are normalised to counter-clockwise winding, so wall normals face into the hole regardless of how the source polygon was wound.

## Rounded rect corners

`corner_radius` is not decoration. `@tscircuit/core`'s `generatePanelTabsAndMouseBites` emits every panel tab cutout as `shape: "rect"` with a rotation and `corner_radius` equal to half the routed slot width — a fully rounded slot. Exporting those as sharp rectangles misrepresents what the router removes, at exactly the tabs someone would measure.

Rect therefore emits four sides plus four quarter-arc corners. The radius is clamped to `min(width, height) / 2` and sides the radius has eaten collapse to nothing, so `corner_radius: 0` degenerates to the sharp-corner boundary and the fully rounded case falls out as a stadium — no separate code path for either. Corners are real cylindrical geometry, not a tessellation a mechanical consumer would have to work around.

Arc circles are placed with a +Z normal so the curve parametrisation already runs counter-clockwise and matches the boundary winding, which avoids the reversed-sense bookkeeping the pill hole geometry needs.

Rect `rotation` is honoured, which is the same property https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/issues/67 reports being lost elsewhere.

## Robustness

- The vertex cache keys on rounded coordinates with `-0` folded into `0`, matching the pill hole cache. A shared corner is reached by two different formulas — the straight side computes it directly, the arc as centre plus radius — so the two can land either side of zero, and `(-1e-16).toFixed(9)` is `"-0.000000000"`. That is enough to split one corner into two vertices and leave the loop open.
- A rect that collapses to fewer than three segments (zero width or height) is skipped rather than built as a zero-area hole, matching the guard the polygon boundary already had.

## Not included: `shape: "path"`

Deliberately, not pending. Nothing in tscircuit emits path cutouts — `Cutout.ts` produces only rect, circle and polygon — the docs don't describe them, and the two existing consumers disagree with the schema and with each other: `circuit-json-to-kicad` draws a bare centerline and `circuit-to-svg` fills `route` as a polygon, neither honouring `slot_width`. Implementing swept slot geometry with no producer and no reference renderer to check against would be guesswork, and the inner-side self-intersection on tight turns has no answer in an exporter with no boolean/CSG. Happy to add it if a producer lands.

## Verification

- `bun test` — 16 passed
- `bunx tsc --noEmit`
- `bun run format:check`
- `bun run build` (including `--dts`)
- Both commits are independently green, so the stack bisects cleanly
- `repro05` covers circle, rotated rect and polygon; `repro06` covers a rotated fully rounded slot as the panelizer emits it, a partially rounded rect, a `corner_radius` larger than the rect, and a zero-height rect
- Coverage is asserted by point-in-triangle tests against the OCCT-imported mesh rather than by grepping the STEP text, so a cutout that fails to pierce the board fails the test
- Confirmed on the real 71.5 mm four-cutout board described above, which now exports with the tower cutouts cut through

## Related

- https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/3302 — original report (gerber + kicad + step). The gerber half is still open.
- https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/pull/330 — the KiCad half of the same issue
- https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/issues/39 — same gap in the GLTF path (outline, holes and cutouts), not addressed here
- https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-tscircuit/issues/67 — rect cutout rotation lost elsewhere

title: fix: shorten rail label connectors to clear nearby traces
description: Fixes rail label connectors to ensure they do not overlap with nearby traces, preventing routing issues in schematic designs.
body:
Late trace rerouting can move a wire through a power/ground label after its connector was placed. In the smart-ring Radio repro, pin 49's GND label extends through pin 45's ground wire despite room above it.

The existing rail-label placement pass now considers shorter endpoints along a dedicated connector's terminal segment. It moves the label and trims the wire together, reuses existing collision checks, and preserves every attached pin, same-net junction, and other label. Candidates are tried nearest to the original anchor first. This works for upward and downward rails without circuit-specific names, IDs, new dependencies, or a new pipeline stage.

Stacked on #1371. The regression now checks that the entire GND label stops above pin 45's trace and that no wire tail remains. The full-sheet SVG snapshot updates dynamically. Generic tests cover both orientations, reversed paths, same/different nets, attachment preservation, obstacles, and missing connector provenance.

The initial default-timeout full run had two existing large fixtures exceed 5 seconds; both passed with the longer timeout.

title: chore: prepare 0.0.68 release containing explicit-pour clipping
description: Updates package.json version from 0.0.67 to 0.0.68 for the next patch release, ensuring that previously merged fixes are included in the npm package.
body:
Ray's tscircuit/core#4703 fix is merged in #126, but npm 0.0.67 predates it. The #128 release-baseline merge changed package.json's version at the tip of main, so pver detects the latest commit as the version commit and exits with "No changes detected". Re-running that same automatic release does not publish the unreleased source fixes.

Prepare the next patch release, 0.0.68, from current main. This is release bookkeeping only: no solver implementation or downstream dependency changes.

Publication sequence after review/merge: create v0.0.68 at the merged release commit, then invoke the existing Publish to npm workflow with release_tag=v0.0.68. That supported recovery path publishes an existing unpublished tag without asking pver to infer another version. Verify npm's artifact contains #126, then invoke the existing downstream package updaters. Merging this PR alone is not evidence that the release has published.

This is a one-time publication recovery for the already merged fixes, not a replacement for automatic downstream dependency updates. Hosted solver tests/type checks run on this PR.

title: Allow custom visualization renderers in GenericSolverDebugger
description: Add an optional customRenderer to GenericSolverDebugger for 3D visualization without coupling to a specific 3D package, while retaining existing 2D functionality.
body:
`GenericSolverDebugger` currently assumes a 2D GraphicsObject, so 3D solvers must project their scene or duplicate the debugger controls. Add an optional `customRenderer` with a name, render callback and visualization download callback. It skips the 2D visualization/empty-state logic while retaining stepping, animation, stats, constructor downloads and pipeline controls. The renderer name replaces the vector/canvas selector.

This enables the new `graphics-debug-3d` viewer without coupling solver-utils to a specific 3D package. Existing 2D callers keep their current behavior.

Validation: all 35 tests pass (197 assertions) on Bun 1.4.4, including a 3D-only solver whose 2D visualization throws; TypeScript and package build pass. The collision checker supplies the browser integration fixture.

React is now an optional peer dependency so the built React entrypoint uses the consumer's React instance. A built-entrypoint rendering check runs in CI to catch duplicate-React hook failures. Browser verification with the collision fixture covers stepping, animation, orbit/zoom/reset and downloading the 3D visualization. The PR preview workflow supplies a reproducible artifact for that downstream integration.

title: Expose configured worker count on solver runtimes
description: Adds an optional read-only workerCount property to SolverRuntimeExecutor to report the configured worker count for shared work queues without modifying runtime properties.
body:
Parent solvers need the host's execution capacity to size shared work queues without adding runtime properties themselves. Add optional read-only `workerCount` to `SolverRuntimeExecutor` and a getter on the shared runtime, inherited by Bun and Node. Inline execution reports 1; threaded execution reports the configured pool size before startup. This is configured capacity, not live worker availability, including after an opt-in serial startup fallback.

The optional interface property preserves compatibility with custom executors. This supports https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3371; after release, that PR's temporary published-package compatibility adapter can be removed.

Validation: all 34 tests pass (192 assertions), including new coverage for inline and both threaded hosts before/after startup. Build, TypeScript, formatting, and packed Node/Bun/browser consumer checks pass locally. Includes the existing Markdown formatting corrections in README.md and CLAUDE.md required by CI.

title: Fix RP2040 bypasses, oscillator network, and ferrite selection
description: Fixes missing bypass capacitors for DVDD pins, updates oscillator network components, and corrects ferrite bead selection for the RP2040 motor-controller circuit.
body:
The [RP2040 motor-controller's common@0.0.48 patch](https://tscircuit.com/imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller/tree/patches) repairs support-circuit defects still present on main: neither DVDD pin has its own 100 nF bypass, XOUT drives the old crystal directly without the reference series resistor, and L_AVDD's supplier entry does not identify the intended BLM18AG601SN1D bead.

Port the reusable electrical corrections: add C_DVDD1/C_DVDD2 with direct pin connections and GND returns; select ABM8-272-T3 with its actual 10 pF load specification, two 15 pF load capacitors and a 1 kΩ XOUT series resistor; select BLM18AG601SN1D/C19330. Keep both sides of the new series resistor in the first routing phase and require zero vias. The new crystal wrapper uses the downstream supplier-imported pad geometry and model reference; the existing X322512MSB4SI wrapper is unchanged.

The oscillator and bypass network follow [Raspberry Pi's hardware design guide](https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/rp2040/hardware-design-with-rp2040.pdf), §§2.1.2 and 2.3, and [Abracon's specifications](https://abracon.com/datasheets/ABM8-272-T3.pdf). This changes the selected crystal and its accompanying network together, rather than relabeling the old part's load capacitance. [LCSC confirms the bead selection](https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C19330.html).

### Motor-controller reproduction

`tests/fixtures/rp2040-motor-controller.circuit.tsx` reduces v1.0.48's real four-layer controller integration, preserving its MCU/group placement, controller sheet and STEP/DIR connections while importing this upstream module instead of the project's patched vendor replacement. Its three electrical tests fail against original main and pass with this change. They inspect rendered components, physical-pin connections, bypass returns, oscillator values, absence of a direct resistor bypass, and the ferrite BOM entry. Native PCB/schematic snapshots and reproduction instructions are committed alongside it.

These are reproduced design/metadata defects, not measured physical hardware failures. Board-specific sheet special cases, global net/group changes, saved-route paths and wholesale placement changes from the downstream patch are excluded. The downstream motor board's saved routing plan is not reused or rerouted.

### Validation

- `bun test`: 22 pass, 0 fail; the three new tests all fail on original main.
- TypeScript, library JS/declaration build, full source formatting and `git diff --check` pass.
- Native PCB/schematic snapshots updated for the reproduction, reusable module and USB-C example; existing module/example 3D snapshots refreshed. The routed PCB SVGs are recorded from CI to preserve its floating-point serialization.
- A routed 30 × 70 mm instance of the updated module completes with 101 traces and zero circuit error records.

![Motor-controller-derived reproduction](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/common/cc500faee41827c06f86684e4bad8f079a1d4de7/tests/fixtures/__snapshots__/rp2040-motor-controller.circuit-schematic.snap.svg)

title: Render explosion lines from glTF scene extras
description: Adds support for rendering explosion lines from glTF scene extras without adding physical geometry, allowing for better visualization of assembly paths in 3D models.
body:
glTF assets can carry explosion guide paths without adding physical geometry. Read `scenes[gltf.scene].extras.poppygl.explosionLines` and use the existing overlay renderer in the scene, GLB, URL, and legacy Buffer entrypoints. Points are in final glTF world coordinates, so node transforms are not applied again.

Explicit `explosionLines` replaces the embedded paths; `null` or `[]` hides them. Other glTF viewers can ignore the optional extras. This supplies the renderer contract used by [circuit-json-to-gltf #276](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf/pull/276) and [svg.tscircuit.com #2774](https://github.com/tscircuit/svg.tscircuit.com/pull/2774).

Validation: 12 focused tests pass (113 assertions), including selected-scene handling, unchanged geometry, pixel equality with explicit options, overrides, GLB and JSON URL entrypoints, Buffer compatibility, occlusion, clipping, and existing lamp/arrow snapshots. title: repro: NEMA34 global copper-edge clearance is lost
description: Reproduces the issue of lost global copper-edge clearance for the NEMA34 controller due to the exporter dropping the min_board_edge_clearance setting, resulting in unintended DRC errors.
body:
Native GitHub [stack #786](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/stack/786). Merge order: **#784 (repro) → #785 (fix)**. Both branches are in this upstream repository; the fix targets this repro branch.

The project exporter drops `pcb_board.min_board_edge_clearance`. On a reduction of the real NEMA34 controller, the authored **0.20 mm** constraint becomes KiCad's default **0.50 mm**, producing four copper-edge findings at a track with approximately **0.4453 mm** clearance.

This is the reproduction-only part of #755: four unchanged records from [pd1180-epr@952de54](https://github.com/techmannih/pd1180-epr/blob/952de54ca0b5dbe042d9ccc9a1a9ecf3e8f67779/release/circuit.json), provenance, the existing geometry illustration, and native KiCad regression tests. **No production code changes.** Two `test.failing` assertions capture the missing setting and resulting DRC errors; the stacked fix converts them into normal passing assertions. KiCad runs outside those assertions so tool/process failures cannot count as a successful reproduction.

![Actual NEMA34 geometry and edge-clearance comparison](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/7ca6ad4cab118f7828253e8903733db9f715fbf2/tests/assets/nema34-board-edge-clearance.png)

The image plots fixture geometry, not a KiCad GUI screenshot. The before/after illustration previews the stacked fix; this repro branch still produces four edge findings.

Local typecheck reports the existing `AddNetsStage.ts:93` dependency-type incompatibility, verified identical on the upstream baseline.

This global board rule is separate from the GND pour's 0.50 mm inset. This focused repro does not certify the entire board. Merge this reproduction before its stacked fix.

description: Avoids unnecessary net lookups for empty grid cells and eliminates redundant path-state allocations for dominated arrivals in the A01 autorouting algorithm.
body:
A01 looks up net metadata for empty grid cells on every expansion and allocates full path-state objects for arrivals that an earlier, no-worse queued arrival will cause it to skip.

Check occupancy before net lookups. Retain dominated arrivals' heap priority, tie order, and iteration slot, but omit their redundant path-state allocation. Search budgets and routing decisions stay unchanged.

The captured motherboard workload retains all 10,627,203 iterations and its exact outcome hash. Full-board timing and dataset 18 validation are tracked in the autorouter integration PR.

Supersedes the exploratory compact-candidate approach in #135.

title: Add exact prepared routing with SolverRuntime geometry preparation
description: Moves the exact-output port-point optimization from tscircuit-autorouter into tiny-hypergraph, adding an opt-in PreparedPortPointRoutingSolver with cached segment distances and route-local available-neighbor lists.
body:
Move the exact-output port-point optimization from [tscircuit-autorouter #3305](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3305) into tiny-hypergraph, which owns the topology, candidate heap, region costs, and rerip state.

Adds opt-in `PreparedPortPointRoutingSolver`, with cached segment distances, route-local available-neighbor lists, and marginal region cost tables. Native search order, floating-point addition order, heap ties, partial routing, rerips, final acceptance, and iteration budgets are preserved. Existing solver classes retain their behavior. The stable-initial-assignment subclass moves with the optimization.

Static distance preparation uses the standard `SolverRuntime` convention and `@tscircuit/solver-utils >=0.0.23` as a runtime dependency. Applications supply their existing executor and import `tiny-hypergraph/lib/prepared/RegionDistancePreparationSolver` in their worker entrypoint before `SolverRuntime.listen()`. Serial mode runs the same preparation inline. Results are assembled in submission order and worker errors propagate.

**Search and route commits remain serial.** The speedup primarily comes from cheaper search operations, not four-way search scaling. Tables are capped at 128 MiB; general incidence and non-dense queues retain native expansion.

Validation:
- All 163 upstream tests pass locally (161 in the full run; two subprocess tests rerun successfully after placing Bun on PATH).
- Full TypeScript check passes.
- Moved tests compare original, serial, one-worker, and four-worker results with pool reuse, forced final acceptance, nonzero density cost, reversed completion order, iteration limits, general incidence, and worker errors.
- No algorithm changes from the implementation benchmarked in autorouter commit `1ebfab8`: [dataset18 benchmark](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3305#issuecomment-6434935073) completed 16/16 samples with zero relaxed DRC errors at both thread counts. Four-thread summed port-point time fell 42.4%; full-pipeline time fell 16.5%; memory P90 rose 12.5%. Those timings predate the package extraction.

The companion [autorouter PR #3305](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3305), commit `6477b55`, pins this PR's exact commit `ec80c91ccbf6529bfd9ae5b205c1d24c7f40bef1` and retains pipeline integration, worker registration, and integration coverage.

After extraction, **all 16 dataset18 samples pass locally with four workers, zero relaxed DRC errors, no failures/timeouts, and byte-identical port-point output against the original baseline manifest**. The autorouter's full TypeScript check, package build, eight runtime integration tests, and built Node package four-worker parity/cleanup also pass. Upstream CI tests, type check, and formatting all pass.

title: Detect scattered filtered voltage divider networks
description: Detects excessive separation between two divider resistors and their grounded shunt capacitor in filtered voltage divider networks.
body:
The filtered battery divider in [Devesh36/pocket-audio-player](https://tscircuit.com/Devesh36/pocket-audio-player#schematic) remains scattered after the existing resistor-rotation advice is applied. Extend `VoltageDividerPlacementSolver` with `VoltageDividerNetworkNotGrouped` to report excessive separation between the two divider resistors or their grounded shunt capacitor.

**Stack:** `main` → #386 (repro) → this PR. Merge #386 first; this PR targets its repro branch.

### Before / after

The comparison starts after existing orientation fixes, preserving the published component positions. The corrected native TSX groups all three components, preserves values and pin-to-net connections, and draws continuous wires. Complete-extract analysis reports **0 issues**.

![Filtered divider before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/75af1b95e2afe9428c3fd76cc17b36830dd5cc16/tests/cases/__snapshots__/filtered-voltage-divider-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

</details>

### Scope and reference

Recognizes an explicit supply-to-ground two-resistor divider with one capacitor from its tap to the same ground. Requires a shared local schematic scope and valid, unambiguous geometry. Skips ladders, other branch types, missing rail metadata, DNP/DNC components and overlapping bodies. Compact bends and offsets are accepted; the threshold is a schematic spacing allowance, not a PCB constraint.

[Raspberry Pi Pico datasheet, Appendix B, Figure 19 (PDF page 26)](https://datasheets.raspberrypi.com/pico/pico-datasheet.pdf#page=26) shows **R5/R6/C3** grouped as a filtered VSYS divider. The reference supports the arrangement, not identical values or mandatory exact alignment. The original published extract is retained in #386; no reference images are committed.

The new check also identifies a separated divider in the existing grow-cabinet fixture; its assertion and snapshot now record that finding.

- Generated comparison and full-network SVGs visually inspected; red diagnostics and a central divider are included.
