No tests or publishing commands were run. The actual authenticated release must be confirmed by the publish workflow after merge.

title: Detect backward inductor diode branches at chip junctions
description: Detects backward inductor diode branches at chip junctions, ensuring proper grouping of inductors, diodes, and chip pins to avoid circuit errors.
body:
Stack: repro #377 → this solver. Merge #377 first.

`InductorDiodeGroupingSolver` reports `InductorDiodeNotGrouped` when a diode's connected end faces away from both an inductor and their common chip pin, creating a substantial backward branch. This recognizes the missed U10/L2/D3 layout from Fieldkit.

Detection requires one typed inductor, one typed diode and one chip pin on a private nonrail junction, with the inductor/diode outer terminals on distinct explicitly declared supplies. It validates geometry and local scope and skips DNP/DNC components, shared junctions, missing/conflicting rail evidence, compact bends and branches that face either peer. No names or labels establish electrical roles, and the rule works for every drawing axis.

The native TSX correction puts the three components around a clear shared junction. D3 retains its original symbol, orientation and polarity. All electrical connections, component values and chip pins are preserved, and the complete three-component extract reports zero findings. Tests also verify continuous drawn wires to both peers.

![Before and after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/fix/inductor-diode-grouping/tests/cases/__snapshots__/inductor-diode-grouping-correction-comparison.snap.svg)

[Complete corrected extract](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/fix/inductor-diode-grouping/tests/cases/__snapshots__/inductor-diode-grouping-correction-full-network.snap.svg)

Source: [gokul/fieldkit-usb](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/fieldkit-usb#schematic), release 0.4.2, `sections/display.tsx`.

Reference: [Aerosemi MT3608 datasheet, page 1, Figure 1](https://www.olimex.com/Products/Breadboarding/BB-PWR-3608/resources/MT3608.pdf#page=1). L1, D1 and SW form a compact T junction. That drawing uses a horizontal diode; this correction retains a vertical diode. The shared-junction convention is the reference, not an exact orientation. Reference media is not committed.

Validation: `bun test` — 300 pass, 0 fail; `bun run typecheck`; `bun run format:check`. Guard coverage includes names-independent topology, explicit port supply metadata, all rotations/reflections, missing/conflicting rails, extra junction members, shorted devices, invalid/duplicate geometry, scope, DNP/DNC components and compact alternatives. title: Detect resistor dividers placed behind connected chip pins

body:
Repair can reduce reported DRC errors by creating a physical short between previously separate nets. Add a physical trace-contact guard to output publication and safe checkpoints, plus bounded local repair for pipeline-owned deferred contacts. The guard accounts for copper width, layers, connectivity aliases, route fragments, jumper spans, and contacts cleared by preceding stages.

Stacked on [reproduction #182](https://github.com/tscircuit/high-density-repair03/pull/182). Consumer integration: [autorouter #3353](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3353). Current repair commit: `11a0b354e57c2e23fcbdf11e95bdc1136f50cd9c`.

Candidate checks reuse stationary copper, detect in-place geometry changes, and preserve terminal/jumper boundaries. Redundant via excursions can be simplified only with physical-contact, pad-overlap, and DRC checks. An explicit portfolio-handoff signal lets the consumer retain regional repair when the portfolio finishes normally.

Validation: 154 local repair tests, both TypeScript projects, and current CI pass. Full consumer regressions retain SRJ33 sample003 at 7 DRC errors / 112 vias and Game Boy at 28 DRC errors / 144 vias. Independent exported-copper comparison for Game Boy removes three physical contact pairs and introduces none; pre-existing contacts remain.

Still draft: all four latest same-machine datasets preserve per-sample DRC results, completion/timeouts, and via counts against base, but the strict runtime requirement is not met. Across the predetermined three runs, SRJ18 median P50 delta is +3.91% and Dataset01 median P95 delta is +2.81%. SRJ33 P95 is +0.61%; Game Boy's odd-angle count changes from 1397 to 1409. Full run links and measurements are recorded in the consumer PR.

title: test: reproduce force repair introducing a peer trace short
description: Reproduces a DRC error scenario where a new physical short is introduced between two signal traces while reducing the overall DRC errors.
body:
A four-route input lets `GlobalDrcForceImproveSolver` reduce native DRC errors from five to four while creating a new physical short between `signal_1` and `signal_4`. The pair was separate in the input. Endpoints and the input routes remain unchanged.

The fixture was independently generated and reduced to four three-point routes with decimal coordinates. It runs the native evaluator with the existing 16-iteration budget. An exhaustive segment-distance oracle compares physical contact pairs before and after repair, without relying on DRC messages or generated error IDs.

Only the final no-new-contact assertion uses `test.failing`. Setup, existing input contacts, solver completion, endpoint preservation, input immutability, and non-increasing DRC count are checked in `beforeAll` and fail normally. A stacked fix will convert the assertion to an ordinary passing test.

Validation: the ordinary assertion fails with exactly the new `signal_1`/`signal_4` pair on main `550e7644`; with the expected-failure marker the full local suite passes (139 tests, 0 failures). Both TypeScript projects, formatcheck, and `git diff --check` pass.

title: Avoid repeated FIFO cache eviction scans in the DRC engine
description: Reduces the overhead of cache eviction in the DRC engine by retaining an advancing entry iterator, improving performance during cache churn without altering existing cache behavior.
body:
DRC cache eviction repeatedly created a Map iterator at the beginning of a large, churning cache. Retain an advancing entry iterator for each cache, and reset the query iterator when connectivity invalidates its cache. FIFO order, retained entries, memory accounting, cache keys, and geometry checks remain unchanged.

The captured motherboard power-phase joint repair input, replayed in fresh Bun 1.4.2 processes in baseline–PR–PR–baseline order, took 17.509 / 11.717 / 11.297 / 17.369 seconds. Mean joint repair time fell from 17.439s to 11.507s (34.0%); indexed DRC evaluation fell from 9.931s to 3.927s (60.5%). All four new-route SHA-256 hashes and non-timing repair statistics match.

Complete motherboard routing also improved: 104.592 / 95.056 / 96.433 / 101.477 seconds, reducing the mean from 103.034s to 95.745s (7.1%). Every full output hash, solver iteration count, trace count, and existing DRC finding count matches. Raw measurements and integration are in https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3358.

Validation: all 139 tests pass (40,388 assertions), including FIFO churn, variable entry sizes, full eviction, connectivity invalidation, and cached-versus-uncached DRC parity. Both TypeScript checks pass; CI is green. No wall-clock thresholds or geometry changes.

title: Fix shared runtime peers and verify two-package TI installs
description: Fixes npm installation issues by ensuring exact shared peer versions for tscircuit and circuit-json, preventing import errors and installation conflicts.
body:
Fresh npm installations can select an old Circuit JSON package beside TI while tscircuit installs its compatible schema package elsewhere. Core then imports a missing `source_component_misconfigured_error` export, blocking generation and publication of the watcher.

Use exact shared peer versions that agree with tscircuit's own dependencies, and matching development versions:

```json
{
  "tscircuit": "0.0.3035",
  "@tscircuit/props": "0.0.714",
  "circuit-json": "0.0.537"
}
```

The user-facing install names only TI and tscircuit. Align props with tscircuit instead of requiring the older 0.0.712 copy. npm and Bun resolve props, Circuit JSON, React, and TypeScript automatically. The package-consumer regression now installs exactly those two packages, removing the previous explicit TypeScript install.

Existing projects must remove or update conflicting direct pins once; TI does not rewrite their package.json. Rishabh's board has an unused `circuit-json@^0.0.522` pin. The clean board rehearsal removes that obsolete pin; it does not add props or Circuit JSON directly.

- Reproduced the original publication failure before the fix.
- Format, typecheck, and all 78 Node CLI tests plus 3 Bun snapshot tests pass.
- Node 24 package-consumer checks pass with only TI and tscircuit explicitly installed, including CLI/watcher use, TSX conversion, TypeScript, ESM/CJS rendering, and isolated global installation.
- A fresh `imrishabh18/pedometer@1.1.6` Bun installation naming only the local TI distribution and tscircuit automatically resolves props 0.0.714 and Circuit JSON 0.0.537. Neither is a direct dependency in the prepared board manifest.

The board rehearsal uses the locally packaged PR build. Published TI 1.0.11 still lacks `watch-sysconfig`; the normal npm workflow requires this PR to merge and a new release to publish.

title: Add ti watch-sysconfig for automatic RunFrame updates
description: Saving pin attributes should update the SysConfig page already open in RunFrame. This adds ti watch-sysconfig file to the installed TI executable. It buildsgenerates the source, encodes a new viewer URL, and updates the matching extraRunFrameTabs entry in tscircuit.config.json.
body:
Saving pin attributes should update the SysConfig page already open in RunFrame. This adds `ti watch-sysconfig <file>` to the installed TI executable. It builds/generates the source, encodes a new viewer URL, and updates the matching `extraRunFrameTabs` entry in `tscircuit.config.json`.

### Usage

Run these together in a board project:

```sh
tsci dev ./index.circuit.tsx
ti watch-sysconfig ./index.circuit.tsx
```

The board owner can manually combine them into `bun run dev` using `concurrently --kill-others`; the [watch guide](docs/watch-sysconfig.md) includes the package script. This PR ships the TI command and documentation. No bundled board/demo, public tscircuit CLI changes, configuration hooks, private viewer dependency, or local TI SDK installation is introduced. Existing one-shot generation commands remain unchanged.

### Behavior

- Generates once on startup and after source/imported pin-attribute saves. Also accepts Circuit JSON or an existing `.syscfg` and watches that file directly.
- Debounces and serializes builds, discards superseded results, and ignores generated/config writes.
- Preserves other configuration settings and tabs; circuit inputs scope the tab to that board.
- Errors retain the last successful preview. Successful updates are quiet. Ctrl+C stops watching and terminates build subprocesses.
- Currently supports macOS/Linux with JSON project configuration. Module-based configuration is rejected explicitly rather than overwritten.

### Verified live behavior

Tested against `imrishabh18/pedometer@1.1.6`, published `tscircuit@0.0.3003`, and the deployed viewer. Changing `U1.pin9` from Output to Input updated the open iframe automatically, with the SysConfig tab and pin selection retained. No browser reload or pin reselection was used after the edit. The original pin attributes were restored afterward; the board itself is not committed.

Before saving:

![Pin 9 before the source edit](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/blob/04268d3a8aa0fd2bc21254c80d9035e44fe035ac/.github/pr-assets/automatic-sysconfig-preview/before-output.png?raw=true)

After saving:

![Pin 9 automatically updates to Input](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/blob/04268d3a8aa0fd2bc21254c80d9035e44fe035ac/.github/pr-assets/automatic-sysconfig-preview/after-input.png?raw=true)

### Validation

- 78 Node CLI tests and 3 Bun snapshot tests pass, including 11 numbered watcher tests.
- Watcher coverage includes file edits, atomic Circuit JSON replacement under `dist`, stale-build rejection, error recovery, config preservation, quiet output, and subprocess shutdown.
- Root format and typecheck pass. A clean install with Bun 1.4.4 passes all 78 Node CLI tests and 3 Bun snapshot tests.
- The [package CI job](https://github.com/tscircuit/ti/actions/runs/40591394467/job/122496269746) passes on `505cabc`, including CLI tests and clean local/global npm consumer checks.
- Aligns the development versions of tscircuit, Core, props, Circuit JSON, and SVG with the tscircuit 0.0.3031 release. The previous mixed versions nested dependencies outside the CLI's resolution path and produced incompatible utility exports. No dependency overrides, extra packages, or weakened checks were added.

Existing Markdown formatting in three documents was normalized for the configured formatter. This verifies configuration preview updates; it does not perform TI solver validation or establish PCB manufacturing readiness. The upstream board has existing PCB errors.

Package, format, System Block UI, and Vercel checks pass on `505cabc`. The separate `tscircuit/build` status is pending and is not part of this package-check fix. There are no tracked demo files or changes to the build workflows.

title: Allow a completed expansion-pass budget before cleanup
description: Adds maxExpansionPasses option to allow callers to finish a complete widening pass before cleanup, improving autorouter performance without changing default behavior.
body:
Add `maxExpansionPasses` (default four) so callers can finish a complete widening pass and proceed to cleanup instead of spending the entire iteration budget on diminishing-return retries. Keep the per-segment inflation attempt limit independent of the pass limit. Invalid non-positive or non-integer limits throw.

This enables a separate autorouter performance experiment: on the motherboard, one completed pass retained widening work and reduced relaxed DRC errors from 1,307 to 1,303, with no error category increasing. Local timing is exploratory; an isolated end-to-end benchmark belongs to the integration PR. Default behavior is unchanged.

Validation: all 99 tests pass (139,844 assertions), including completed cleanup, retained expansion and invalid limit cases; TypeScript and package build pass. Stacked on #65.

title: Prepare net-specific collision indexes once per grid search
description: Prepares net-specific collision indexes once per grid search to optimize routing performance by reusing unchanged geometry predicates, reducing redundant calculations and improving efficiency.
body:
Grid searches repeatedly resolve the same net exemptions and clearance rules while querying a board-wide layer index. Prepare an index of nearby blocking copper once per search, then reuse the unchanged exact geometry predicates for each segment. The prepared index belongs to that search; there is no cross-search cache. Out-of-region segments throw. Routing order, costs, budgets and clearances stay unchanged.

Paired fresh-process baseline–PR–PR–baseline runs on Bun 1.4.2/macOS arm64:

| Measurement | Base mean | PR mean | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Complete motherboard routing | 105.047s | 98.658s | −6.1% |
| Power expansion | 26.181s | 20.836s | −20.4% |

The four complete times were 103.019 / 99.894 / 97.422 / 107.076 seconds. All four produce the same output SHA-256 (`5c90f0d5e4bd73b4aed32d62e1f4350e5df0f36a70c53d47a2a79d714d7ab974`), 761 traces, 10,652,531 iterations, and the same 1,300 pre-existing relaxed DRC findings. No snapshots changed.

Separate operation-count runs (not timing measurements) show board-wide source-index queries falling from 13,832,743 to 1,449,438 and rule evaluations from 37,933,395 to 17,849,194. Per-segment local-index searches still occur; these numbers do not claim that all spatial searching disappeared. Both diagnostic expansion outputs and iteration counts match.

Validation: all 95 tests / 39,791 assertions, existing snapshots, type checking and the package/declaration build pass locally. Tests compare ordinary and prepared queries across layers, nets, trace exclusions, holes, vias and exact boundaries. Existing grid-route fixtures retain their exact paths and iteration counts. Vercel is green; this repository has no GitHub Actions test workflow.

Autorouter adoption: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3366, with green CI and seven focused local integration tests. This targets the integration branch currently consumed by the autorouter.

`/benchmark --dataset 18` completed: 16/16 solved and passed relaxed DRC, no timeouts, no outcome regressions, and identical non-timing routing metrics. Median runtime was 34.6s → 33.8s; P80 was 72.7s → 76.8s. Recorded stage totals were effectively unchanged (712.709s → 711.724s). Power expansion totaled only about 0.001s in either revision, so these timing fluctuations do not measure this optimization. The motherboard comparison above exercises the changed path.

title: Scope boolean collision searches to the queried copper layer
description: Scopes boolean collision searches to the queried copper layer, reducing unnecessary spatial candidates and improving query performance.
body:
Boolean collision queries in motherboard bugreport110 retrieved 129,982,687 spatial candidates; 82,097,138 (63%) were immediately rejected for being on another layer. Build per-layer indexes lazily for boolean queries so unrelated copper is not retrieved. Through-vias remain in every occupied layer. Keep the original global index and ordering for collision-list, contact and drill queries.

Four fresh-process, unprofiled runs of the same captured expansion input in baseline/changed/changed/baseline order measured 24.206/21.942/21.921/24.321 seconds: 9.6% less expansion time. This is a stage-only gain of about 2.3 seconds, not a 9.6% full-board speedup. All runs produced identical output and 7,751,939 iterations. Peak RSS varied from 2.21 to 2.46 GiB; the run set is too small to claim a memory improvement.

Validation: all 92 existing tests pass without snapshot updates; a new differential test adds 5,605 assertions across layers, nets, rotated obstacles, holes, ignored route ranges, through-vias and board bounds. Build and TypeScript checks pass. The companion autorouter PR contains the probes and measurement artifacts under numbered bugreport110.

Based on the merged #62 integration branch to preserve the autorouter's existing safety fixes. No change to collision geometry, route effort, iteration budgets, or search ordering.


The companion PR is [autorouter #3356](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3356). Its complete motherboard output remains byte-identical and all CI checks pass. Dataset 18 completed all 16 boards with no routing-outcome regressions, but median time increased 5.1% and P90 increased 2.6% in its single paired control; no broad runtime improvement is claimed. The targeted expansion replay above is the measured benefit.

title: Index rectangular obstacles by exact geometry and reuse unchanged solver statistics
description: Rectangular obstacles are now indexed as one bounding box with their exact rotated polygon, independent of size or electrical purpose. This replaces the copper-pour-specific Infinity cell-size shortcut. The broad-phase index filters candidates; the existing exact geometry predicates still decide collision and physical contact. Oval approximation, circular holes, layer rules, alias resolution, object IDs and padviahole clearances are preserved.
body:
Rectangular obstacles are now indexed as one bounding box with their exact rotated polygon, independent of size or electrical purpose. This replaces the copper-pour-specific `Infinity` cell-size shortcut. The broad-phase index filters candidates; the existing exact geometry predicates still decide collision and physical contact. Oval approximation, circular holes, layer rules, alias resolution, object IDs and pad/via/hole clearances are preserved.

Two board-sized planes previously generated 110,538 cells on every rebuild. They now require two entries. The implementation applies equally to rectangular pads, keepouts and other obstacles. It also retains the parent-statistics reuse optimization from #36 with original authorship and its tests.

Validation:
- 92 dependency tests pass (25,703 assertions); build and TypeScript checks pass.
- Tiled-versus-exact comparisons cover pours and non-pours, rotations, layer exclusion, same-net blocking, physical contact, and pad/via/hole clearance boundaries.
- The complete motherboard solve is byte-identical to the original expander on the same macOS runtime: `5c90f0d5e4bd73b4aed32d62e1f4350e5df0f36a70c53d47a2a79d714d7ab974`.
- Three debug snapshots change the spatial-index bounds overlay/framing. All routed trace coordinates are unchanged. The autorouter reproduction snapshots are unchanged.

The previous unprofiled measurement was 56.09 -> 28.33 seconds for expansion and 174.84 -> 107.33 seconds for the complete power-phase pipeline including the preload fix. Those timings precede this generalization; they are not new measurements of this revision. Dataset 18 completed on tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3345 with this dependency pin: all 16 samples completed and passed relaxed DRC on both revisions, with no routing-outcome regressions. P50 time decreased 1.7%, P90 time decreased 4.3%, and P90 memory increased 8.2% in the single paired run. Dataset 18 barely exercises power expansion; the direct tests remain essential. [Results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3345#issuecomment-6501178855). All autorouter CI checks pass, including exact full-output equality against the original expander on Linux.

Based on the autorouter's original `01ce270` dependency, retaining its connectivity, immutable-copper and declared via-pad-clearance guards.

description: Fixes the NEMA23 models wire exit orientation to prevent misalignment with the rear screw axes, ensuring compatibility with rear-mounted controllers.
body:

Pin Biome to 2.5.9 and match its configuration schema. The repository does not save a lockfile, so the previous caret range installed Biome 2.6.4 in CI and introduced formatting failures across existing Markdown files.

The solver rejects any nonempty board outline, including the unchanged outline of the real OrangeCrab r0.2.1 ECP5/DDR3L PCB, before starting routing. Add the shared real KiCad-derived capture and the outline repros only. Independently pin the exact 19 removed trace IDs and 22 via IDs; compare every unrelated PCB element against the original and verify both complete capture SHA-256 hashes. Preserve six layers, 163 components, all pad/hole coordinates, original copper, native routing layers and captured DDR constraints. Document the intentionally castellated J1/J2 headers. **Reproduce and focused validation:** `bun test tests/repros` — 5 tests pass. **Stack:** [#110](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/110) → [#107](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/107) → [#111](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/111) → [#108](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/108) → [#112](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/112) → [#109](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/109). This PR targets main. Next: #107. | Before: Completed rectangular positive control | After: Same completed control; production unchanged | | --- | --- | | ![Before: Completed rectangular positive control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/5e91c430694fa0b2bc67e5e712e325cf640eec70/tests/repros/__snapshots__/routing-positive-control-pcb.snap.svg) | ![After: Same completed control; production unchanged](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/5e91c430694fa0b2bc67e5e712e325cf640eec70/tests/repros/__snapshots__/routing-positive-control-pcb.snap.svg) | Both panels intentionally show the same fully routed synthetic control. The real OrangeCrab outline failure is described in text and produces no routing image. Solver source is identical to main in this repro. All shown SVGs use the single shared `toMatchPcbSnapshot` adapter backed by `circuit-to-svg` and `bun-match-svg`; no custom SVG drawing/exporter is added. Snapshots are written only after solved/nonfailed state, complete endpoint connectivity, native copper DRC, applicable bus bounds/pair skew/coupling/spacing, and unchanged input/fixed copper are checked. Each displayed SVG was visually inspected. Failed/unrouted diagnostics remain local. **Scope and limitations:** This is a test/fixture-only reproduction; it does not change production solver behavior. The unchanged real OrangeCrab outline can be accepted after #107, but its full DDR lane still has native-approach routing failures. Small completed synthetic controls do not establish complete OrangeCrab routing, timing closure, impedance or hardware validation. Original capture geometry, copper and constraints are preserved. **Snapshot dependencies:** Keep only the existing renderer/matcher's required development dependencies: `circuit-to-svg@0.0.453`, `bun-match-svg@0.0.17`, `@tscircuit/alphabet@0.0.25`, and `schematic-symbols@0.0.248`. The renderer's combined entry point imports its declared peers even for PCB SVGs. `circuit-json@0.0.538` is needed for its `getSimulationReturnCurrentGridJsonSchema` export; the previous 0.0.514 fails the renderer import. Production exports and tarball isolation are checked with `bun run test:package`. No unrelated package versions or export paths are changed.\n\n**Final-head validation:** Bun 1.4.0. `bun install`, `bun test --timeout 120000` (532 pass, 0 fail), `bun test tests/repros` (5 pass, 0 fail), `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run test:package` all pass on head `5e91c430694fa0b2bc67e5e712e325cf640eec70`. The full suite also passes in CI using the repository’s existing 120-second default test budget. Bare `bun test` was run and hits the unchanged H3 test’s five-second default timeout; no unrelated timeout or assertion was changed. All final-head CI checks, including fresh `AM3352 benchmark (11/11)`, are green. This PR remains draft and unmerged. **Benchmark comparison:** [Final-head Blacksmith workflow and raw paired artifacts](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/40957759276). Exact base `ead4eb9db255118af9713136abb16e4d72e5c36c`; head `5e91c430694fa0b2bc67e5e712e325cf640eec70`. **Independent final-head artifact audit** The paired workflow runs the benchmark engine used by `./benchmark.sh`; the pinned base harness runs fresh base and head workers serially per sample, alternating order. Both use identical input hashes and the same Bun/runtime, runner class, GC settings and 3,600-second budgets. title: fix: support board outlines
description: Fixes the rejection of valid PCB outlines and introduces validation for openclosed simple polygons, ensuring continuous copper-capsule clearance in routing.
body:
Valid PCB outlines were rejected with `Custom board outlines are unsupported`. Endpoint-only containment also cannot detect a segment crossing a concave cutout or copper whose width/via land reaches outside an edge. Validate open/closed simple polygons in either winding; enforce continuous copper-capsule clearance in vector/grid search and final trace/via acceptance. Cover concavity, exiting/reentering segments, self-intersections, degeneracy, trace width, via-land diameter, exact endpoints and input immutability. The board-edge regression uses the same geometry as `tscircuit-autorouter/tests/drc-board-edge-debug.test.ts` and independently calls the existing native board-edge checker. New geometry helpers use named arguments. **Reproduce and focused validation:** `bun test tests/repros tests/board-outline.test.ts` — 22 tests pass. **Stack:** [#110](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/110) → [#107](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/107) → [#111](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/111) → [#108](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/108) → [#112](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/112) → [#109](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/pull/109). This PR targets #110. Next: #111. | Before: Completed rectangular positive control | After: Completed concave-outline regression | | --- | --- | | ![Before: Completed rectangular positive control](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/5e91c430694fa0b2bc67e5e712e325cf640eec70/tests/repros/__snapshots__/routing-positive-control-pcb.snap.svg) | ![After: Completed concave-outline regression](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/0dac23a3987026c367e03d7febc5fc68d4ea4a4c/tests/repros/__snapshots__/concave-board-outline-pcb.snap.svg) | The inputs differ: the before control has rectangular bounds and no cutout; the after regression uses the concave outline rejected by the baseline. Both panels show accepted, complete routes; neither depicts completed OrangeCrab DDR routing. All shown SVGs use the single shared `toMatchPcbSnapshot` adapter backed by `circuit-to-svg` and `bun-match-svg`; no custom SVG drawing/exporter is added. Snapshots are written only after solved/nonfailed state, complete endpoint connectivity, native copper DRC, applicable bus bounds/pair skew/coupling/spacing, and unchanged input/fixed copper are checked. Each displayed SVG was visually inspected. Failed/unrouted diagnostics remain local. **Scope and limitations:** This validates one simple polygon, including concave notches/cutouts; it does not add a multi-ring outline format. The real-board regression checks outline acceptance, and the separate small concave regression checks complete routing. The unchanged real OrangeCrab outline can be accepted after #107, but its full DDR lane still has native-approach routing failures. Small completed synthetic controls do not establish complete OrangeCrab routing, timing closure, impedance or hardware validation. Original capture geometry, copper and constraints are preserved. **Final-head validation:** Bun 1.4.0. `bun install`, `bun test --timeout 120000` (549 pass, 0 fail), `bun test tests/repros` (5 pass, 0 fail), `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run test:package` all pass on head `0dac23a3987026c367e03d7febc5fc68d4ea4a4c`. The full suite also passes in CI using the repository’s existing 120-second default test budget. Bare `bun test` was run and hits the unchanged H3 test’s five-second default timeout; no unrelated timeout or assertion was changed. All final-head CI checks, including fresh `AM3352 benchmark (11/11)`, are green. This PR remains open and unmerged. **Benchmark comparison:** [Final-head Blacksmith workflow and raw paired artifacts](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/actions/runs/40957762140). Exact base `5e91c430694fa0b2bc67e5e712e325cf640eec70`; head `0dac23a3987026c367e03d7febc5fc68d4ea4a4c`. **Independent final-head artifact audit** The paired workflow runs the benchmark engine used by `./benchmark.sh`; the pinned base harness runs fresh base and head workers serially per sample, alternating order. Both use identical input hashes and the same Bun/runtime, runner class, GC settings and 3,600-second budgets. title: fix: support named colors and align PCB text fonts and layout
description: Adds support for named colors in PCB annotations and corrects text sizinglayout and font rendering for SVG reference images.
body:
PCB annotations using named colors such as `white` or `red` were omitted with an `Unsupported color` diagnostic. This PR adds named-color support and also corrects PCB note text sizing/layout and the font used to render SVG reference images.

The scope includes:

- **Named colors:** accept CSS color names, case variations, surrounding whitespace, and `transparent`, while preserving existing hex/RGB/RGBA parsing. In the via-board-tenting example, previously missing white labels now appear.
- **PCB note sizing and layout:** match SVG font advances and baselines, anchor multiline notes to the first line, use one font-size step between lines, and keep bottom-layer notes upright unless explicitly mirrored.
- **SVG reference font:** explicitly load the TscircuitAlphabet font already embedded by `circuit-to-svg` into Resvg. This replaces system-font fallback in the reference images and changes their visible font appearance and sizing.
- **Parity comparison:** compare both base and proposed WebGPU output against the same current SVG image. Regression tests verify that worsened GPU output still fails; comparison tolerances remain unchanged.

For snapshot review, start with the [via-board-tenting comparison](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/blob/5ac3fc29741ee832ead4bbfdd97ea12cfbd7f6b8/tests/snapshots/features/pcb-via-board-tenting-f28cd3a1d048.png): SVG is on the left and WebGPU is on the right. The color fix restores missing white text rather than recoloring existing labels. Other updated snapshots reflect the font, sizing, and layout changes described above, including Linux variants.

Validation on `5ac3fc2`:

- [Renderer CI passed](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/actions/runs/40682477403): formatting, typecheck, 119 unit tests, build, visual checks, 597 feature snapshots with zero failures, and layout checks.
- [Parity audit passed](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/actions/runs/40682477419): zero new regressions across 597 comparisons. Strict SVG mismatches decrease from 383 to 380 against the shared reference; 12 pre-existing upstream reference failures remain.
- All 148 CSS color keywords were verified against their expected RGB values.

title: Publish WebGPU automatically on main updates
description: Automatically triggers publishing of a renderer release on pushes to the main branch, while maintaining manual source-ref releases and ensuring the latest tag is used to prevent exhausting the tag retry limit.
body:
Merging changes into main currently does not publish a renderer release. Trigger publishing on pushes to main, while retaining manual source-ref releases and checking out the exact triggering commit.

Seed the release version from the latest tag because release commits are not pushed to main; this prevents repeated automatic releases from exhausting pver’s ten-tag retry limit. Existing validation, serialized publishing, registry, and tag publishing remain in place.

Validation: actionlint and git diff --check pass. The existing publish workflow successfully released the merged blind/buried-via fix.

title: Fix missing blind and buried via drill markers
description: Fixes missing drill markers for blind and buried vias in the rendering process, ensuring accurate representation in the AM3352 board.
body:
Blind and buried vias had their holes erased from copper but never received pink drill geometry: the compiler only painted drills when the span contained both top and bottom. The supplied AM3352 board has 113 affected vias out of 918.

Compile partial-depth drill markers by copper span and apply the selected-layer/hidden-layer opacity to those spans. Through-hole substrate removal stays unchanged. Preserve drill color overrides, explicit drill filters, silkscreen text compositing, and X-Ray selection for the new drill groups.

Validation:
- 120 unit tests pass, including 10 new span/detail regression cases (8 failed before the fix).
- Format, TypeScript, and production build pass.
- WebGPU visual suite passes on SwiftShader, including pixel checks on top, bottom, and inner layers; explicit filters; and X-Ray selection.
- Updated the dense inner-layer via snapshot and 61 feature snapshots for newly visible blind/buried drill centers. Explicit copper filters limit the new markers to their physical span, including when hidden-layer opacity is 1. Covered partial-depth drill markers hide when solder mask is shown, and X-Ray still exposes selected drills. The dense top-layer snapshot remains unchanged.
- Pin Linux SVG fallback to DejaVu Sans in both base and head audits; update 15 SVG reference halves to remove dependence on system font enumeration. Candidate renderer comparisons and pixel thresholds are unchanged.

The linked static site bundles an older renderer and will need a dependency update/rebuild after this fix is released. This fixes confirmed missing partial-depth drill markers; I did not reproduce an intermittent disappearance of every through-via drill.

title: Reproduce AM3352 traces hidden by solder mask
description: Reproduces a bug where the AM3352 DDR_ODT trace is hidden beneath the WebGPU solder mask, providing a comprehensive test for the issue.
body:
0hmx@dots

The AM3352 DDR_ODT top trace is present in the compiled copper but disappears under WebGPU's solder mask. Canvas displays covered copper in a distinct mask color; disabling the mask in WebGPU reveals the trace.

Source: AM3352 board [commit 99b75cf](https://github.com/0hmX/am3352-ddr-track-a-local-dfm-wip-20261007/tree/99b75cf9844894b4ad65ee9cb4669b6bcf575d88), [DDR_ODT route](https://github.com/0hmX/am3352-ddr-track-a-local-dfm-wip-20261007/blob/99b75cf9844894b4ad65ee9cb4669b6bcf575d88/data/ddr-routes.tsx#L1095), [route emission](https://github.com/0hmX/am3352-ddr-track-a-local-dfm-wip-20261007/blob/99b75cf9844894b4ad65ee9cb4669b6bcf575d88/layout/DdrRoutes.tsx), and [F5 via](https://github.com/0hmX/am3352-ddr-track-a-local-dfm-wip-20261007/blob/99b75cf9844894b4ad65ee9cb4669b6bcf575d88/layout/DdrPowerConnections.tsx#L3). The pinned Canvas reference [renders traces using its mask-over-copper color](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-canvas/blob/fa8405c67634e287b79a1506eedde077ef6accb0/lib/drawer/elements/pcb-soldermask/trace.ts). This native TSX fixture preserves the DDR_ODT endpoints, 0.1 mm width, top layer, eight-layer board, and a board-derived F5 via. The test checks the specific current defect: the trace is present in copper geometry but absent from mask paint, while pad and via openings are retained. It deliberately describes the current behavior and will be inverted by the fix.

Validation: `bun test tests/am3352-soldermask-trace.test.ts` and `bun run typecheck` passed. The original board was compared visually in pcb-viewer 1.11.435 with matching top-layer settings. This regression checks compiled geometry, not GPU pixels; the exact embedded WebGPU package version in the board preview is unverified.

CI: `test:snapshots` failed twice with 15 cases (0000, 0004, 0009, 0011, 0031, 0498, 0512, 0533, 0534, 0546, 0559, 0565, 0566, 0577, 0585). In [parity attempt 1](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/actions/runs/40697054804/attempts/1), the unmodified base and reproduction each failed exactly these same 15 snapshots on Ubuntu image 20261025.353.1. In [attempt 2](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/actions/runs/40697054804/attempts/2), both passed all 597 snapshots on image 20261012.334.1; the parity check passed. The same two image versions correlate respectively with the failed reproduction renderer job and the passing fix renderer job. The logged direct package versions and Playwright browser build match; no tracked lockfile guarantees transitive versions. The image association is evidence, not proof of which environment component caused the drift. The failed cases include text, pad-mask coverage and margins, hole margins, and panel vias. The reproduction changes no renderer, audit setup or snapshots. No unrelated goldens were updated.

Merge order: merge this reproduction first, then the stacked fix PR #96.

### WebGPU visual comparison

The native DDR_ODT fixture is rendered at both PR heads with the same top layer, camera and 800 × 700 canvas in the Codex in-app browser using Apple Metal 3. With solder mask enabled, the trace disappears before the fix and is visible in the covered-copper color after it. Both endpoint pads and the F5 via remain visible.

title: fix: accept pcb_stackup metadata without stopping PCB rendering
description: Fixes the issue where PCB rendering stops due to unsupported pcb_stackup metadata by adding it to the allowlist, allowing eight-layer boards to compile without diagnostics.
body:
Stacked on #90. Add `pcb_stackup` to the existing non-rendered metadata allowlist. An eight-layer board with `fabricatorPreset="jlcpcb_standard"` now compiles without diagnostics, so pcb-viewer's WebGPU worker can display it. Unsupported shapes still produce diagnostics through the existing error path.

Where to look:
- `lib/compile-circuit.ts`: the only runtime change is one allowlist entry.
- `tests/pcb-stackup.test.ts`: replaces the reproduction's expected error with no diagnostics, nonempty geometry, unchanged triangle count, and identical vertex/index buffers when input element indices are held stable.
- `tests/fixtures/pcb-stackup.tsx` in #90 is the source of the board; no hand-authored Circuit JSON.
- `tests/snapshots/pcb-stackup/before.png` is replaced in place: GitHub's image diff shows the failing preview on the base and the working preview on this branch.

![Before: WebGPU rejects stackup metadata](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/codex/repro-pcb-stackup-metadata/tests/snapshots/pcb-stackup/before.png)

![After: actual pcb-viewer WebGPU worker renders both resistors and their trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/codex/fix-pcb-stackup-metadata/tests/snapshots/pcb-stackup/before.png)

Validation (the runtime change passed CI, including all feature snapshots and the base/head parity audit):
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run test` (111 pass), and `bun run build` pass.
- `WEBGPU_SOFTWARE=1 bun run test:visual` passes the full renderer visual suite. The hardware-mode run failed when Chromium lost its adapter during repeated device creation; software mode runs real WebGPU shaders with SwiftShader.
- Local macOS full feature audit: 590/597 goldens pass; all seven mismatches also fail on untouched main with its original dependencies, with byte-identical SVG/WebGPU PNGs for the seven cases. Linux CI passes all feature snapshots. The local 597-pair report layout check passes at desktop and mobile widths.
- Packed this renderer locally, installed the tarball into an isolated pcb-viewer 1.11.436 checkout, and rebuilt its release bundle. The actual bundled worker now completes a frame with no errors on the same TSX-generated input. Canvas also completes without errors. #90 captures the zero-frame failure before the fix.

The runtime change is +1 line; this stacked code diff is 10 added / 13 removed lines, plus the existing reproduction screenshot updated in place.

Release dependency: pcb-viewer currently pins circuit-json-webgpu 0.0.10. Publish the fixed renderer after review, then update pcb-viewer's jscdn tarball pin and lockfile. The local verification tarball is deliberately not a permanent dependency. No changes were made to the shared DDR board checkout or its running preview.

title: test: reproduce pcb_stackup metadata breaking native PCB previews
description: Reproduces a bug where the pcb_stackup metadata causes the WebGPU compiler to report unsupported geometry, halting the rendering process in the pcb-viewer.
body:
An eight-layer `<board fabricatorPreset="jlcpcb_standard">` emits `pcb_stackup`. The WebGPU compiler reports it as unsupported geometry, and pcb-viewer's worker stops before its first frame. Canvas renders the same board correctly.

This is the reproduction PR. The stacked fix is #91, which replaces the assertion of the current diagnostic with a regression asserting unchanged geometry and no diagnostics.

Where to look:
- `tests/fixtures/pcb-stackup.tsx`: native TSX source, two 0402 resistors and one routed trace. Circuit JSON is generated by core, never hand-authored.
- `tests/pcb-stackup.test.ts`: asserts an eight-layer board, four pads, a trace, and the exact `pcb_stackup` diagnostic. Removing only the generated metadata clears that diagnostic.
- `lib/compile-circuit.ts`: the existing non-rendered metadata allowlist is missing `pcb_stackup`.
- pcb-viewer's `src/lib/webgpu/pcb-webgpu.worker.ts` makes any diagnostic fatal.

Confirmed the affected live CLI bundle identifies itself as pcb-viewer **1.11.433**. Also reproduced with current pcb-viewer **1.11.436**, bundling circuit-json-webgpu **0.0.10**. Producer: tscircuit **0.0.3031**, core **0.0.2217**. Added those dev dependencies for repeatable TSX rendering, aligned the older shared helper/schema versions they require, and enabled JSX/ES2023 type checking for core's declarations. The frozen Canvas reference tests retain circuit-json-util 0.0.99 through a development-only alias and link in `tests/parity/prepare-upstream.ts`, so core's newer helper does not change their camera bounds or golden images. Runtime dependencies are unchanged.

Actual pcb-viewer screenshots (same generated input):

![Before: WebGPU stops on pcb_stackup with zero frames](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/codex/repro-pcb-stackup-metadata/tests/snapshots/pcb-stackup/before.png)

![Canvas control: both resistors and the connecting trace render](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/codex/repro-pcb-stackup-metadata/tests/snapshots/pcb-stackup/canvas-control.png)

Validation: latest CI `test` and `parity` jobs both pass. `bun run test` — 111 pass; `bun run typecheck` passes. Browser check: WebGPU zero frames/zero completions with the exact error; Canvas one completion and no error.

To inspect interactively, use sibling checkouts of this branch and pcb-viewer, run `bun tests/fixtures/pcb-stackup.tsx > ../pcb-viewer/tests/webgpu/actual/stackup.circuit.json` (create the ignored `actual` directory first), then run pcb-viewer's build and Vite. Open `/tests/webgpu/?circuitJsonUrl=/tests/webgpu/actual/stackup.circuit.json`, adding `&scenario=canvas` for the working control. The generated JSON is only a transport artifact; the TSX is the reproduction source.

title: fix: use type-only fanout paths for browser imports
description: Fixes import failure in the online editor by using type-only fanout paths and removing runtime parsing calls.
body:
Importing the package in the online editor fails because the package loads the runtime `fanoutTracePath` schema from `@tscircuit/props`, which the evaluator supplies as a type-only shim.

Use `import type { FanoutTracePath }` and type assertions for the checked-in power, signal, and UART route JSON. Remove all three runtime `.parse()` calls so the compiled package can load with the existing evaluator. The saved routing data is unchanged.

Validation:
- `bun run typecheck`
- `bun run build -- --svgs` — all four circuits passed.
- `bun run test`
- Bundled the package as browser CommonJS and verified that it has no runtime `@tscircuit/props` dependency. The original evaluator's compiled-JS loader loads the fixed bundle and creates both `StandardJstSwdResetSide` and `ProgrammerBoard` with the empty props shim; the original published bundle reproduces the failure.
- Verified that all 153 saved paths produce identical autorouting phase props before and after removing the explicit parsing.

Supersedes https://github.com/tscircuit/eval/pull/5476.

title: Add NEMA14 RP2040/A4988 native firmware target
description: Adds native firmware 1.0.20 for the NEMA14 RP2040A4988 PCB, including GPIO assignments and telemetry support for motor control.
body:
Adds native firmware 1.0.20 for the NEMA14 RP2040/A4988 PCB. The existing targets use different GPIO assignments; the new `nema14_a4988` target uses the board's STEP/DIR/enable/sleep pins and generic JEDEC boot for its GD25Q16E flash.

Supports motorcontrol.tscircuit.com jogging, finite/prepared moves, ramps, RGB, buzzer, temperature and supply-voltage telemetry. Adds MCU output-pin readbacks and an optional `MOTOR_FULL_STEPS_PER_REVOLUTION` build setting: 400 for the reference 0.9° motor, or 200 for the user's 14HS13-0804S. Current measurement, software current/voltage selection and stall detection are excluded because the PCB does not provide those interfaces.

Validation: native regression tests, both 200/400-step geometry variants and dashboard tests passed. All four hardware targets compiled during implementation. Firmware was flashed with readback verification, connected to the production dashboard, and the user confirmed that the motor spins. PIO diagnostics counted exact pulses with zero underruns; enabled moves read ENABLE_N=0, SLEEP=1 and about 14.9 V. No extra motion guards were added in the diagnostic follow-ups. Loaded accuracy, phase current, transients, thermal-trip behavior and waveforms remain unmeasured.

title: Build multilayer Palace geometry without 3D Booleans
description: Stacked on 19 (featmultilayer-surface-impedance, the version simulate.tscircuit.com deploys).
body:
Stacked on #19 (`feat/multilayer-surface-impedance`, the version simulate.tscircuit.com deploys).

## Problem

The multilayer mesher fragmented overlapping copper, dielectric and air solids in one global OpenCascade Boolean. On dense DDR crops all the memory went there, before any mesh existed. AM3352 `DDR_CSn0` was killed above 6 GB locally, and failed on hosted 12 GB, 64 GB and 128 GB machines.

## Change

`mesh_multilayer.py` no longer runs any 3D Boolean:

1. Build a disjoint 2D material partition for each z interval (copper per net, dielectric, air).
2. Overlay every interval into one planar arrangement, snap-rounded to a 0.5 µm grid (`SLIVER_MM`). A fixed-precision union guarantees noding, and grid-scale and sliver cells join their neighbours.
3. Build the B-rep by hand in the built-in kernel:
   - Faces exist only where materials change. Coplanar horizontal faces and stacked lateral faces merge.
   - Volumes are connected same-material regions.
   - A check rejects any non-conforming interior edge.
4. Lumped ports (vertical, slanted and coplanar) become embedded faces on protected cut lines. Slanted apertures are split into one exactly planar quad per z step.

Material ownership is unchanged: copper wins, drilled holes and outer-foil gaps are air, and inner-foil gaps belong to the slab above.

## Results (mesher only, 400 MHz, surface-impedance copper, dialog 4-layer defaults)

| AM3352 crop | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `DDR_DQSn1`, 0.25 mm margin | 31 s, 3.9 GB, min SICN 3e-6 | 14 s, 0.8 GB, 236k tets, min SICN 2.3e-3 |
| `DDR_CSn0`, 0.25 mm margin | killed above 6 GB in the OCC fragment | 55 s, 2.9 GB, 877k tets, min SICN 8.7e-4 |
| `DDR_CSn0`, 1 mm margin | hosted 12/64/128 GB failures | 81 s, 3.8 GB, 1.18M tets, min SICN 2.3e-4 |

Comparing the meshed physical groups on `DDR_DQSn1`, old against new:
- air and dielectric volumes are within 2.5e-5 relative;
- copper conductor areas are within 4.3e-4 relative, since sub-micron slivers are removed;
- the 45° port is 0.22% narrower after snapping;
- centroids are within 0.24 µm.

## Tests

- `tests/palace/boolean-cleanup.*` covered the removed OCC fragment cleanup. They are replaced by `tests/palace/layered-geometry.*`, which checks meshed dielectric volumes and port areas against the planar partition, and minimum SICN, for the surface, cropped and volume variants. The CI workflow is updated.
- The Palace mesh CI set passes locally.
  - On macOS, gmsh 4.13.1 segfaults at interpreter exit in about half of runs (exit 139, after writing outputs). This happens before and after this change, so local runs needed retries.
  - The surface sampler (vtk import timeout) and `multilayer-reference` fail locally on the unmodified branch too.
- `tsc --noEmit` passes.

## Not verified

- No Palace field solve has run on the new meshes yet; only the mesher was exercised.
- Comparing return-current fields on `DDR_DQSn1` between old and new meshes is the remaining check.

title: Publish the built adapter through GitHub Packages and JSCDN
description: Publish a built tscircuitjscad-to-manifold package through GitHub PackagesJSCDN to allow core to depend on a versioned release instead of building from a GitHub commit during installation.
body:
Core currently consumes this adapter from a GitHub commit and must build it during installation. Publish a built `@tscircuit/jscad-to-manifold` package through GitHub Packages/JSCDN so core can depend on a versioned release instead.

The package includes ESM, CommonJS and TypeScript declarations. Remove the Git-install `prepare` hook, build during packing, and add a release workflow triggered by a matching version tag. `jscad-planner` becomes a wildcard peer with a concrete development version; earcut is already bundled and stays development-only. Manifold continues to be injected and is not a runtime dependency.

Validation: frozen install, type checking, all 18 tests (90 assertions) and both builds pass. A packed clean npm install with scripts disabled passes ESM/CommonJS hole-geometry checks and consumer TypeScript checking; its dependency tree contains no `manifold-3d`.

Core integration: https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5011.

Release `0.0.1` has now been published from tag `v0.0.1` by [the successful release workflow](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-to-manifold/actions/runs/41541150337). The JSCDN tarball returns 200 and includes both runtime formats and declarations. Installation directly from JSCDN with scripts disabled passes the same ESM, CommonJS and TypeScript consumer checks.

title: Separate regression tests from release artifact builds
description: Refactors the CICD pipeline to separate regression tests from the release artifact builds, optimizing the build process and reducing build times significantly.
body:
Manual and daily releases previously invoked all of CI, then built and verified an unsigned Windows installer before repeating that work for the signed installer. Releases now call a dedicated reusable build workflow and proceed directly to signing after artifact qualification.

The Tests workflow (ci.yml, retaining its manual dispatch entry point) owns typechecks, the prototype UI build, unit/regression suites, native macOS installer fixtures, PowerShell compatibility/timeout tests, negative Authenticode cases, and unsigned Windows installer verification. Unit tests run alongside artifact builds. Signature rejection tests use the signed Microsoft PowerShell host, without release credentials.

The reusable build prepares embedded assets once and compiles all five targets in parallel. Linux x64 runs the actual CLI and offline browser checks in its target job, alongside the other builds; this removes a duplicate Linux compilation and the second non-browser smoke run. Cache Bun package downloads by OS, runtime and dependency graph.

Keep selected-version offline browser/worker/WASM qualification, native signed executable startup, signed installer verification, signing/notarization receipts, and checksum checks in the release path. Windows runtime checks run against the signed executable once. No change to signing identities, notarization requirements, publication gating or release assets.

Measured with tscircuit 0.0.3050: the new release build path completed in 4m14s, versus 11m26s for the previous builds plus unsigned installer gate, about seven minutes less before signing. These are observed qualification timings; signing and Apple service time are additional.

Validation:
- [Standard PR CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41454273229) passed.
- [Full 0.0.3050 qualification](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41454291398) passed: 221 unit/regression tests, four platform-specific skips, five builds, offline browser checks, Linux archive installation, both native Mac checks, PowerShell/signature tests and unsigned Windows installer verification.
- `bun run test tests/sign-macos.test.ts tests/daily-release.test.ts tests/prepare-release.test.ts`: 48 passed locally. actionlint and diff checks passed. No release was published or protected signing job invoked by these qualifications.

Stacked on #43 to retain its bounded installer waits and diagnostic uploads. Merge #43 first, then retarget this PR to main.

title: Bound Windows installer verification and retain diagnostics
description: Implements bounded process waits for Windows installer verification, adds diagnostics logging, and ensures timely cleanup and reporting of installer operations.
body:
The manual release and its retry stop in Windows installer verification and exceed the job's 30-minute limit, so signing and publishing are skipped. Dependency preparation, offline browser checks and all five platform builds pass with tscircuit 0.0.3050. Original run: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41427099965

A build-only qualification reproduced a stall after starting the installer upgrade. GitHub no longer serves the original canceled job's log blob, so the underlying Windows startup cause is not established. This change removes unbounded process-tree waits, avoids creating a console for unattended commands, and adds launch/exit timestamps. Installer operations have three-minute deadlines; version and rollback checks have one-minute deadlines. Timeouts terminate the process tree and identify the failed operation. Cleanup restores PATH even if uninstall fails.

A ten-minute smoke-step fallback leaves room to upload diagnostics before the job limit. Save the transcript, stdout/stderr and Inno Setup logs outside the disposable install directory, and upload them on success or failure in both unsigned qualification and signed verification. Signing and notarization requirements remain unchanged.

Validation:
- Full build-only qualification of the final revision with tscircuit 0.0.3050 passed: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/actions/runs/41450098820. All five platforms and offline browser checks passed; real Windows install/conflict/version/upgrade/uninstall/rollback verification completed in 53 seconds.
- One focused native regression script covers exit codes/output with spaced paths, a completed parent with a live child, and timeout termination of a hung process tree. It passes in both pwsh and Windows PowerShell 5.1.
- `bun run test tests/build-windows-installer.test.ts tests/windows-bootstrap.test.ts`: four pass, one Windows-only skip on macOS. Workflow YAML parsing and diff checks pass.

After merging, start a new manual release from main so it uses the updated workflow. Re-running the old release retains its original commit. The later daily release's Apple ticket-service network failure is a separate transient signing issue.

title: Update CLI to 0.1.2427 and embed dependency versions
description: Updates the standalone binarys direct tscircuitcli dependency to version 0.1.2427 and embeds dependency versions during compilation to resolve issues with CI smoke checks.
body:
Update the standalone binary's direct `@tscircuit/cli` dependency from `0.1.2410` to `0.1.2427`, including the merged datasheet-search support from https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5628.

The newer CLI looks up dependency versions from installed package manifests when rendering `tsci dev`. A compiled standalone binary has no `node_modules`, so this caused the CI smoke check to fail with `Cannot find package 'tscircuit'`.

Extend the existing standalone build adapter to resolve literal dependency-version queries during compilation and embed the installed values. Versions are read through the bundled tscircuit runtime's dependency graph; none are hardcoded. The TypeScript parser identifies calls without changing string contents, and unsupported dynamic queries fail the build. No shared CLI changes or standalone-specific upstream behavior are needed. Baked-search defaults remain separate in https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-standalone/pull/41.

title: fix: extract ground vias directly contacting pads
description: Fixes ground via connections directly inside reference pads to produce vertical barrel connections to the ground pour instead of failing due to missing routed ground leads.
body:
A ground via directly inside a reference pad now produces a vertical barrel connection to the ground pour instead of failing because there is no routed ground lead. Native vias associated through a source trace are resolved alongside net-bound vias. The extractor checks electrical association, pad contact, declared layer span, barrel dimensions and its contact with the actual pour before generating the FastHenry and FasterCap geometry. An offset via within the pad uses an inscribed strip to model its pad contact.

This is stacked on #17. Review the [top and inner1 views](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/blob/repro/via-in-pad-ground/tests/visual/via-in-pad.md) for the native TSX fixture. The current contact model conservatively supports circular and rectangular pads with the via annulus fully contained and a barrel disk fully inside the pour; partial overlaps and cutout contact are rejected until a more detailed model supports them. Existing routed leads remain supported, with the same span and barrel checks.

Validation: `pnpm test` (156 passed, one skipped); `pnpm typecheck`; focused native tests covering centered and offset contacts, disconnected/wrong-net/ambiguous vias, conflicting span and net metadata, invalid plating, omitted stubs, and a barrel crossing the plane edge. The original eight-layer DDR reproduction's physical records passed schema validation and generated both FastHenry and FasterCap inputs; no native solver run is claimed.

body:
A native DDR-style channel with each ground via centered inside its pad fails extraction because the reference connection requires a routed ground lead. The vias span top to the solid inner1 ground pour, and the native render has no errors.

title: fix: distinguish native process timeouts from solver failures
description: Fixes the reporting of native timeouts in FastHenry by distinguishing them from solver failures, providing clearer diagnostic messages.
body:
When FastHenry exceeds the adapter deadline, report `native_timeout: fasthenry: exceeded 900000 ms process timeout` with the original command and captured stdout/stderr. Previously the message only said `native_solver: ... Command failed`, so a long extraction killed by the adapter looked like a numerical solver failure.

Stacked on #14 (native TSX reproduction and PCB visual). The seven-line diff uses `execFile`'s killed flag, SIGTERM, and null exit code; a self/external signal and output-buffer errors must not be labelled as deadline expiry. Process cleanup, the default deadline, geometry and all numerical acceptance checks stay as before.

Validation: typecheck; full suite (151 pass, one opt-in skip); real FastHenry TSX reproduction (5/5 combined focused tests); focused adapter + real solver tests on Bun 1.3.14; isolated package tests on Node and Bun. The same 6,210-filament refined deck now reports `native_timeout` at the deliberate 100 ms deadline.

This fixes the diagnosis, not a proven FastHenry numerical defect. The original board's 284,695-filament run has not been retried and no complete matrix, transient or eye is claimed. CLI 0.1.2418 bundles the adapter, so its installed bundle needs a pipeline release/dependency refresh to receive this diagnostic fix. [CLI #5620](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5620) → [#5621](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5621) exposes the adapter's existing `timeoutMs` setting. With an explicit 30-second deadline, the identical reduced deck completes in approximately 4.35 seconds and returns all four matrix rows; this is extraction-only evidence, not a validated board eye. The pipeline CI passed at this PR head.

title: test: reproduce native DDR extraction timeout misdiagnosis
description: Reproduces a bug where the native FastHenry process misdiagnoses a timeout as a command failure, adding a regression test and an opt-in reproduction for the FastHenry extraction process.
body:
A native FastHenry process killed by the adapter deadline currently raises `native_solver: ... Command failed`, indistinguishable in the message from an unsuccessful numerical run. This adds a failing process-level regression and an opt-in real FastHenry reproduction built from native TSX.

The reduced fixture renders U1 (left) and U3 (right): DQ, DQS and DQSn are the three horizontal traces; the lower pads/vias are their ground references. Inspect [`tests/fixtures/native-ddr-timeout.tsx`](https://github.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/blob/repro/native-solver-timeout/tests/fixtures/native-ddr-timeout.tsx) and the native PCB rendering below. It retains 640 MT/s, 512 ns, PRBS7 and the original extraction settings (3/5 filaments, 3 mm coarse / 1.5 mm refined ground mesh, unchanged tolerances). Geometry is reduced to straight 12 mm lanes and one reference pour. The test stops at refined extraction; declaration-only IBIS references are never read. No vendor files, cached matrices or eye results are included.

![Native TSX DQ/DQS geometry](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/pcb-spice-pipeline/repro/native-solver-timeout/tests/reproductions/native-timeout/pcb.svg)

Reproduce after `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm build`:
```sh
node --import tsx --test tests/node.test.ts
PCB_SPICE_FASTHENRY=/path/to/fasthenry node --import tsx --test tests/native-timeout.test.ts
```
The ordinary process test runs in CI; the real solver test is opt-in. Both deadline assertions fail on this branch (`native_solver` versus expected `native_timeout`). The real FastHenry run was bounded to 100 ms and reached Multipole Summary with 6,210 filaments. Typecheck passes.

Origin: AM3352 board commit `99b75cf9844894b4ad65ee9cb4669b6bcf575d88`, CLI 0.1.2418. Its preserved refined input reached 284,695 filaments, and the reported duration matches the adapter's 900,000 ms limit. That historical timeout remains an inference; no numerical failure is proven by its truncated log. This reproduction proves the adapter diagnostic defect, not full-board convergence. The fix is stacked in #15. The CLI deadline control is tracked in [CLI #5620](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5620) → [#5621](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5621).

title: Reject incompatible or unassociated native via metadata
description: Rejects incompatible or unassociated native vias by enforcing trace association and rejecting mismatched physical layers, ensuring valid hole diameters for vias in PCB designs.
body: The native via resolver could take a hole diameter from an unrelated co-located physical via, or accept an inline diameter while ignoring an associated via whose layers do not span the route. Require trace association before using physical dimensions and reject mismatched physical layers even when the route supplies a hole. This is stacked on #11, whose native TSX fixture and visual snapshot show the via-in-pad channel and reproduce both failure modes.

body: Extends the existing visual native TSX via-in-pad reproduction with the board’s 0.2 mm hole, 0.3 mm diameter and top-to-inner2 layer checks. Two regression cases show that a co-located unrelated via can supply the hole, and an inline hole can hide incompatible physical layers. The fixture is native TSX; the cases alter its generated metadata to exercise malformed associations. Both new tests fail on main. The existing visual evidence is in tests/reproductions/native-channel/before.svg. A stacked fix follows.

body:
Fixes the three native TSX channel-preparation failures in #8, which is this PR's base. Resolve via dimensions from associated `pcb_via` records, keep channel endpoint nodes distinct when both pins share an unambiguous net binding, and use Clipper2 integer-grid copper booleans to handle the sampled bend. Input route vertices and solver acceptance thresholds stay unchanged.

title: Reproduce native DDR via, channel-cut and copper-union failures in TSX
description: Reproduces failures in native TSX board output during channel preparation related to via dimensions, net bindings, and copper union precision, enabling further debugging and fixes.
body:
Native TSX board output fails during channel preparation in three cases: via dimensions stored in `pcb_via`, component bindings that join both channel endpoints to one net, and a three-point copper bend that breaks the polygon union.

This reproduction PR is the base for #9. The three tests render `tests/fixtures/native-channel.tsx` and assert the current failures. The core/props dev dependency update enables native fabrication stackups.

title: Add standalone test-point rerouter and PD power supply prototype
description: Adds a standalone test-point rerouting solver for designated routed traces. It places exposed probe pads on the requested outer layer, checks copper clearance and probe spacing, and uses bounded local detours when a pad cannot fit directly on the trace.
body:
Adds a standalone test-point rerouting solver for designated routed traces. It places exposed probe pads on the requested outer layer, checks copper clearance and probe spacing, and uses bounded local detours when a pad cannot fit directly on the trace.

The prototype uses the actual astra/pd-power-supply board (pinned release 57387f49-bd91-4277-8a82-706b1575c5ed), adding bottom-side TP_SDA, TP_SCL, and TP_OUTPUT_EN. A negative-control test moves a generated pad onto an unrelated via and verifies detection.

Bootstrapped through tscircuit/create-repo and aligned with the handbook: source exports from lib, plop-generated Biome/Bun/Cosmos configuration and test/typecheck/format/build workflows, disabled lockfile saving, and a pages-based solver debugger. body:
Imported CAD models can render correctly while their triangle boundaries fail solid validation, leaving explosion checks incomplete. This adds `prepareCollisionMesh` using the existing `@tscircuit/jscad@0.0.6` geometry kernel, and keeps visual review on real NEMA17/M3 models.

- Export `createCollisionSolid` for strict validation and caller-owned Manifold construction. Mesh preparation frees its temporary WASM solids and returns serializable geometry without mutating input.
- Pin the original modelcdn NEMA17 triangles that failed validation, with source metadata/hash and reproduction instructions. Tests preserve all four 3 mm × 4.5 mm blind bores, bounds within 0.001 mm and volume within 0.002%, then exercise real threaded M3 insertion against the blind-hole floor.
- Use `@tscircuit/manifold-2d@^0.0.8` for runtime loading and all public/debugger types. This preserves the existing package name and removes the full `manifold-3d` dependency and browser CDN import. Initialization uses the wrapper's singleton and embedded WASM.
- Add standalone Node and real Chromium module/classic blob-worker regressions for lazy initialization, shared instance identity and continuous collision detection without runtime downloads or an adjacent WASM file. CI runs the browser tests.
- Remove eight synthetic snapshots and three synthetic Cosmos pages; preserve their numerical tests. All four remaining visual snapshots use real jscad-electronics/modelprinter geometry, PoppyGL, explicit check status, colliding names and swept volume in mm³.
- Show actual new swept interference in orange with a callout projected from an intersection vertex. Labeled cutaways affect display only. The fit variant explicitly uses 3.02 mm smooth bores; internal motor threads and manufacturing tolerances are not represented.

![Four real threaded M3 bolts fit the motor bores](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/cad-collision-checking/2fce2f5134cb608f90d2d3a2192db542192cda73/tests/__snapshots__/nema17-m3-inserted.snap.png)

![Actual interference at the blind-hole floor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/cad-collision-checking/2fce2f5134cb608f90d2d3a2192db542192cda73/tests/__snapshots__/nema17-m3-blind-hole-floor.snap.png)

Validation: **23 tests / 2,414 assertions and two Chromium blob-worker tests pass**, including all four PNG comparisons; typecheck, formatting and Cosmos production build pass. Zero-clearance stock models retain their small reported mesh interference rather than silently treating it as clearance.

[Core #5011](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5011) uses this shared preparation and the exporter's existing mesh loader. Its original RP2040 assembly improves from 5 to 112 checked CAD models out of 117, with explicit warnings for the remaining five. The continuous-sweep algorithm is unchanged.
CI: tests, typecheck and formatting all pass for `6e86d19`.

title: Prune explosion collision sweeps before expensive mesh unions
description: This PR optimizes collision detection by cropping obstacles to swept bounds and constructing triangle prisms only where interference is possible, significantly reducing computation time for threaded bolt checks.
body:
Threaded bolt checks previously spent almost all their time unioning the entire swept solid: one M3 × 4 bolt generated 18,444 prisms, with ~7.5 s in the union and ~16 ms in the final intersection.

This change crops each obstacle to the swept bounds, rejects clear paths using a conservative envelope, and constructs exact triangle prisms only where interference remains possible. The envelope is only a rejection/filtering step. Collision volumes still come from the original meshes, with continuous translation, holes, grouped movements and exclusion of initially occupied space preserved.

Stacked on #10 (real NEMA17/M3 regression fixtures), which is stacked on #8.

### Measured results

Local macOS arm64 / Bun 1.3.14; same pinned modelprinter meshes. Times include solver construction and solving, excluding model generation, WASM loading and rendering. Single runs, so timings are illustrative rather than CI thresholds.

| Case | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Four M3 bolts fit | 29.440 s | 0.281 s |
| 5 µm offset clears | 8.400 s | 0.066 s |
| 20 µm offset hits wall | 8.377 s | 1.432 s |
| M3 × 6 hits blind floor | 12.055 s | 1.594 s |
| Collision between clear endpoints | 7.386 s | 4.756 s |
| Nominal zero-clearance overlap | 7.554 s | 3.833 s |
| Withdrawal from initial overlap | 6.037 s | 0.866 s |

Four clear bolt paths construct zero individual prisms instead of 73,776. The browser debugger completes that case in 0.257 s and still finds the blind-floor collision in 1.665 s. Complex interference still requires synchronous exact CSG and can take several seconds.

### Validation

- 19 tests / 2,362 assertions pass, including the existing real meshes, 5 µm clearance, 20 µm interference, rotated motor movement, tunneling, initial overlaps and grouped stages.
- Retain the old sweep as a test-only reference. Compare total and spatially partitioned collision volumes for 24 deterministic rotated, hollow and disconnected scenes; add full-containment regressions.
- Add a deterministic work regression asserting that all four full-mesh clear paths skip prism construction.
- All 12 PoppyGL snapshots pass. Refresh the blind-floor snapshot after visual inspection because the intersection has different triangulation; its collision volume and location are preserved.
- Typecheck, format check and Cosmos production build pass.
- Add the handbook-style `./benchmark.sh`, with `--help`, `--limit`, `--sample`, `--repeat`, optional PoppyGL snapshots, per-run logs/JSON and avg/P50/P95 durations. All 8 benchmark cases report expected collisions; P50 0.866 s, P95 4.756 s.

title: Test real NEMA17 and threaded M3 mesh collisions
description: Add regression coverage using actual modelprinterJSCAD-electronics NEMA17 and helical M3 bolt meshes, including tests for various collision scenarios and mesh interactions.
body:
Add regression coverage using actual modelprinter/JSCAD-electronics NEMA17 and helical M3 bolt meshes. Bounding boxes are only the broad phase; the tests exercise continuous mesh sweeps without replacing the models with primitive proxies or decimating them.

The nine new tests cover all four mounting holes, 5 µm versus 20 µm lateral offsets, a moving motor in a rotated scene, collisions between clear endpoint poses, the blind-hole floor, and existing-overlap semantics. Four PoppyGL snapshots and a selectable GenericSolverDebugger fixture show the real assembly and display-only cutaways; collision checks always use the entire motor.

The stock NEMA17 has smooth 3 mm bores, not internal threads, and its nominal zero-clearance fit with an M3 bolt contains microscopic mesh overlaps. Keep that diagnostic covered. The separately labeled fit variant explicitly uses 3.02 mm bores (10 µm radial clearance); no collision tolerance was loosened. Full threaded sweeps take several seconds per bolt.

Validation: 16 tests / 89 assertions pass; all 12 PoppyGL snapshots pass; typecheck, format check, and Cosmos production build pass. Browser verification confirms four-bolt insertion with zero collisions and a long-bolt floor collision with the orange intersection visible.

Stacked on #8 so this uses the released solver-utils dependency.

![Actual M3 bolt hitting the NEMA17 blind-hole floor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/cad-collision-checking/feat/nema17-bolt-mesh-collisions/tests/__snapshots__/nema17-m3-blind-hole-floor.snap.png)

title: Use PoppyGL collision snapshots and interactive 3D debugging
description: Replace flattened XYXZYZ SVG snapshots with eight PoppyGL PNG snapshots and a 3D GenericSolverDebugger, enhancing the visualization of collision detection in CAD assemblies.
body:
Replace flattened XY/XZ/YZ SVG snapshots with eight PoppyGL PNG snapshots and a 3D GenericSolverDebugger. `visualize3d()` emits serializable meshes, movement paths, labels, stable program bounds, and optional `cameraPosition`/`cameraTarget`. Moving solids are blue, stationary obstacles are translucent gray, and orange geometry is the actual swept intersection. The collision algorithm is unchanged.

The interactive view uses Three.js/OrbitControls for orbit, pan, zoom, six axis views, fit/reset, and copying a camera fixture. It preserves manual navigation during stepping and animation. Camera fields are part of the visualization output and its JSON download, while remaining outside the collision problem. The grouped fixture shares one authored camera with its three PoppyGL stage snapshots: assembled, cover and bolt lifted together, then the bolt removed through the bracket.

Dependencies: merge/release [graphics-debug-3d #1](https://github.com/tscircuit/graphics-debug-3d/pull/1) and [solver-utils #54](https://github.com/tscircuit/solver-utils/pull/54), then replace pinned GitHub/PR-preview dependency specs with released versions before merging. The graphics-debug-3d override resolves its unreleased peer dependency during review; no local file dependencies are used. This PR remains draft for that release transition.

Validation: seven tests / 48 assertions, eight PNG snapshots, TypeScript, formatting and Cosmos production build pass against the remote review packages. Browser verification covers orbit, keyboard pan, zoom, top-axis view, fit/reset, camera export and playback to completion. Camera coordinates stayed identical through all 14 solver steps. Downloaded visualization contains the authored camera, four meshes including the intersection, and three movement guides.

Preserve movement-only collision semantics, continuous sweeps through thin obstacles, holes/concavities, grouped targets, duplicate-target deduplication, and accumulated movement. Core retains model conversion, stage-membership expansion, incomplete-geometry warnings, and Circuit JSON diagnostics.

Follow the handbook with Bun, TypeScript source exports, no lockfile, plop CI/release templates, and three React Cosmos `GenericSolverDebugger` fixtures. Publish the versioned package through GitHub Packages/jscdn. Repository provisioned by tscircuit/create-repo#103.

body:
Introduce serializable `GraphicsObject3d` meshes, world-space movement lines, labels, bounds, and authored `cameraPosition`/`cameraTarget` fields. PoppyGL renders deterministic PNG snapshots without a browser; the React viewer uses Three.js and OrbitControls for GPU rendering and navigation. Both consume the same scene and camera fixture.

The interactive viewer supports orbit, pan, zoom, six axis views, fit, reset to the authored camera, and copying camera JSON back into a visualization result. Geometry updates and resizes preserve manual navigation; changes to authored camera values apply the new fixture. Render-option cameras override scene cameras for snapshots. Browser lighting/text and PoppyGL rasterization can differ.

Created through [create-repo #104](https://github.com/tscircuit/create-repo/pull/104), following handbook source-package and Cosmos conventions. The source package includes its Three.js types and supports consumer JSX transforms. Picking, editable geometry and scene hierarchies remain outside this initial API.

Validation: four tests / 21 assertions, three PNG snapshots, camera JSON replay and render-option precedence, invalid geometry/cameras, translated mesh bounds and resource disposal, TypeScript, formatting, and Cosmos production build pass. The remote package was installed into cad-collision-checking for browser verification: orbit, keyboard pan, zoom, axis view, fit/reset, camera export, and animation through all 14 solver iterations with exactly unchanged navigation coordinates. All CI checks pass.
